entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document provides a structured regulatory analysis of the City of Los Angeles Existing Buildings Energy and Water Efficiency (EBEWE) Program, codified as Division 97, Article 1, Chapter IX of the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC). The program is administered by the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS). The brief synthesises across the enacted ordinance text, LADBS program guidance, the FAQs for Audits and Retro-Commissioning (A/RCx), and LADWP benchmarking guidance.

Convention notes: The LAMC uses the format "91.97.XXX" while the Los Angeles Building Code (LABC) uses "Chapter 97." These two citation formats reference the same enacted provisions; both are used in the source corpus and both are referenced here. The primary source item is the enacted draft ordinance text. Where the UpCodes published version of the LABC Chapter 97 contains substantive amendments to the original ordinance (Ordinance Nos. 185198, 185586, 185789, and 186480 have amended the original Ordinance No. 184674), those amendments are cited from the UpCodes source and flagged as amendments. Where the LADBS FAQs add procedural specificity, they are cited as Tier 2 regulatory guidance.

Analysis date: 2026. All forward-looking windows are stated relative to this date.

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**What the EBEWE Program Is**

FACT: "This division shall be known as the City of Los Angeles Existing Buildings Energy and Water Efficiency (EBEWE) Program." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT: "It is the purpose of this division to reduce energy and water consumption in buildings, including existing buildings, in the City of Los Angeles. These efficiency improvements will lower the use of energy, water, and greenhouse gas emissions citywide." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

The program has two distinct compliance phases: (1) annual Benchmarking reporting, and (2) Audits and Retro-Commissioning (A/RCx) on a five-year cycle. *Source: LADBS EBEWE Program page, LADBS, current. https://dbs.lacity.gov/services/green-building-sustainability/ebewe

**Effective Date**

FACT (effective_date): "Ordinance No. 184674, effective 1/29/2017, established the EBEWE Program." *Source: EBEWE Ordinances summary, LADBS, last updated 2/28/2023. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/ebewe-ordinances.pdf

**Jurisdictional Scope**

FACT (jurisdictional_scope): the program applies within the City of Los Angeles. The enacted scope provision states: "This division shall apply to all buildings, including existing buildings, that are either: Owned by the City of Los Angeles and are 7,500 square feet or1. more; EXCEPTION: Buildings owned by the City that are less than 15,000 square feet are not subject to the requirements of Section 91.9706. Privately owned and are 20,000 square feet or more;" *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (scope exception — City-owned buildings): "Buildings owned by the City that are less than 15,000 square feet are not subject to the requirements of Section 91.9706" (the audit and retro-commissioning requirements). *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (scope exclusions): "This division shall not apply to one- and two-family dwellings and related accessory structures; residential hotels as defined by the California Health and Safety Code Section 50519; broadcast antennas; vehicle charging stations; utility pumping stations; treatment facilities; sound stages; structures primarily used for the production and post-production of motion pictures and television, and similar uses; and other buildings not meeting the purpose of this division, as determined by the Department of Building and Safety." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

*Analytical inference:* FACT (amendment — Treatment Facility defined): The amended code added a definition: "TREATMENT FACILITY. A facility where industrial processes take place for the treatment of substances, which include, but are not limited to, water, waste, sewage, rain water, oil, and chemicals. Paper mills, foundries, and similar operations are also covered by this definition, which is restricted to the building or buildings where the treatment takes place." *Source: LABC Chapter 97, UpCodes (reflecting amendments through Ordinance No. 186789, effective 11/12/2020). https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

**Clarification on the 20,000 sq ft threshold**

FACT: "Correction: Section 91.9703. Scope in EBEWE Ordinance 184674 (Item 1 below) stated '…Privately owned and 20,000 square feet or more…' However, Sec. 91.9708.1.4 Schedule for Benchmarking Report Compliance in Ordinance 184674 (Item 1) and 185198 (Item 2), stated '…with gross floor area greater than 20,000 square feet …'. Clarification: This section in both Ordinances includes buildings that are of 20,000 square feet…'" *Source: EBEWE Ordinances summary, LADBS, last updated 2/28/2023. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/ebewe-ordinances.pdf

**Why It Applies to the Workspace**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any specific building in the workspace's operational portfolio (as tenant, owner, operator, or other capacity) meets the size thresholds and ownership classification (privately owned, City-owned, or local-agency-owned) that trigger EBEWE obligations is a factual-legal determination requiring review of each building's ownership structure, Certificate of Occupancy square footage, and applicable use classification. The regulation's obligations fall on "the building owner" as defined; the workspace's role relative to any given building must be confirmed by counsel.

Operationally, workspaces that occupy, operate, or manage commercial or mixed-use buildings of 20,000 sq ft or more within Los Angeles city limits should assess whether they, or the building owner, are subject to EBEWE obligations for the current compliance cycle.

---

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

### 1. MONITORING — A/RCx Compliance Cycles Now Active; Next Deadlines Approaching

FACT: "The next A/RCx compliance due date for Building IDs ending in 0 or 1 is still December 1, 2026. • The next A/RCx compliance due date for Building IDs ending in 2 or 3 is still December 1, 2027." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

**Action:** Identify each building's LADBS Building ID (last digit) and map it to the applicable A/RCx compliance due date using Table 9708.2. For building IDs ending in 0 or 1, the December 1, 2026 deadline is five months away as of this brief's analysis date.

*Operational implication:* Energy and Water A/RCx processes each require engagement of a California licensed engineer or architect (specific license types: A — Architect, C — Civil Engineer, E — Electrical Engineer, M — Mechanical Engineer, or S — Structural Engineer), and the audits and retro-commissioning activities cannot be initiated earlier than five years before the compliance due date. *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

---

### 2. ACTION REQUIRED — Annual Benchmarking Report Due June 1 Each Year (Primary Deadline)

FACT (primary_deadline): Under the amended schedule, for privately owned buildings with gross floor area of 100,000 sq ft or more, the annual benchmarking report is "annually no later than June 1" each year; for buildings 50,000–99,999 sq ft, "annually no later than June 1"; for buildings 20,000–49,999 sq ft, "annually no later than June 1st thereafter." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9708.1), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

*Operational implication:* The annual June 1 deadline recurs each year. For workspaces responsible for benchmarking compliance on managed or occupied buildings, the LADWP benchmarking application processing takes 4–6 weeks; the LADWP benchmarking guide recommends data requests no later than March 1. *Source: LADWP Building Benchmarking page, LADWP, current. https://www.ladwp.com/construction-services/building-benchmarking

**Action:** Verify that the annual benchmarking report for the current compliance year has been submitted for each building in scope, and confirm receipt of the LADBS annual disclosure compliance fee payment of $61.00 per building.

---

### 3. ACTION REQUIRED — Noncompliance Fee Exposure

FACT (penalty_summary): "Failure to comply with this division shall subject the owner to noncompliance fees as specified in Section 98.0411 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, except that the amount of the noncompliance fee shall be $202.00." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (late fee multiplier): "Pursuant to L.A.M.C. Section 98.0411 (c), if this invoice is NOT PAID within 30 days of the date of the invoice, an additional 250% late charge/collection fee will be imposed and assignment to a collection agency may be made. After 60 DAYS of NO PAYMENT, interest will accrue at the rate of 12% annually (compounded monthly or portion of a month) until this invoice and any additional charges that have accrued since this invoice was issued have been paid." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

FACT (payment does not equal compliance): "Please note that payment of the non-compliance fee does not result in Compliance. The building will remain out of compliance with the City of Los Angeles and, as with any Los Angeles Municipal Code violation, will be subject to further legal action. Additionally, the status of each building (Complied or Not Complied) is posted publicly and, in the future, may be recorded on the property as an open violation." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating multiple buildings at the 20,000+ sq ft threshold, cumulative noncompliance exposure compounds: the $202 base fee, plus up to 250% late charge, plus 12% annual interest, plus public posting and potential property-level recordation of the violation, creates reputational and transactional risk on property sales or leases.

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

**The Regulation's Obligated Party**

FACT: The EBEWE program's obligations run to "the building owner." The ordinance consistently addresses requirements to "the building owner" throughout Sections 91.9705, 91.9706, 91.9707, and 91.9708. *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether an entity occupying, managing, or operating a building — but not holding title — constitutes "the building owner" under EBEWE, or whether obligations flow to or can be contractually assigned to a tenant, property manager, or operator, is a legal question turning on LAMC definitions and the specific lease, management, or operating agreement in place. Counsel review is required before any workspace assumes or disclaims EBEWE obligations on behalf of a building it does not own.

**Tenant Carve-Outs Within the Base Building Systems Definition**

FACT: "BASE BUILDING SYSTEMS" are defined to exclude: "Systems or subsystems owned by a tenant or for which such tenant bears full maintenance responsibility pursuant to agreement with the owner and that are within the tenant's leased space and/or that exclusively serve such leased space. [and] Systems or subsystems within a tenant's leased space and/or which exclusively serve such leased space and for which the tenant pays all the energy and/or water bills according to usage and/or demand as measured by a meter or sub-meter." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (tenant-space A/RCx exemption conditions): The A/RCx FAQs confirm that a tenant space or entire building fully leased by a single lessee is exempt from A/RCx requirements only if ALL of the following are present: "1. The tenant is fully responsible for maintenance of the energy and water equipment, including HVAC serving their individual space or building. 2. The equipment does not serve areas outside of the tenant space or building (e.g., corridors, lobbies, restrooms, retail space, other tenant spaces, accessory buildings, etc.). 3. The tenant pays the energy (e.g., electrical, lighting systems, and gas systems) and water bills as specified in Section 91.9704 of the LAMC." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

*Operational implication:* For workspaces that are tenants of large commercial buildings in Los Angeles, the carve-out from base building systems — and hence from A/RCx obligations — applies only when all three conditions are simultaneously met. Where common areas, shared HVAC, or shared utilities exist, the tenant-space carve-out is unlikely to apply to the full building. The building owner retains A/RCx obligations for non-exempt areas.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace's lease, utility billing arrangements, and maintenance responsibilities for any specific Los Angeles premises satisfy all three conditions of the Base Building Systems carve-out requires review of the specific lease terms and building configuration by counsel.

**Record Transfer on Sale**

FACT: "When the building is sold, the records shall be given to the new building owner." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

*Operational implication:* For workspaces involved in real estate transactions (acquisitions, dispositions, or sale-leaseback arrangements) involving Los Angeles commercial buildings of 20,000+ sq ft, EBEWE compliance records (five years of benchmarking data, audit and retro-commissioning reports) form part of the building's compliance record and transfer obligations. Due diligence on EBEWE compliance status is relevant to any such transaction.

---

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

### LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026)

The LADBS has published an A/RCx FAQ document that constitutes Tier 2 regulatory guidance. Key provisions relevant to the workspace:

**COVID Tolling Period — Now Closed**

FACT: "The tolling of deadlines due to the COVID pandemic was in effect from March 21, 2020 through February 28, 2023." Notices to comply were reissued following rescission; most reissued notices indicated a compliance due date of September 7, 2023 or October 7, 2023. "The tolling of deadlines did not affect the designation of A/RCx Compliance Years and all future Compliance Due Dates are according to the schedule of compliance in Section 9708.2 of the LAMC." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

*Operational implication:* The COVID tolling window is closed. All future compliance is on the standard five-year cycle per Table 9708.2 based on LADBS Building ID last digit.

**Submission Window for A/RCx**

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "Reports or requests for exemption must be received by LADBS by the compliance due date, but not earlier than 90 calendar days prior to the compliance due date." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9708.2), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

**Licensed Professional Requirement**

FACT: The valid license types for the architect or engineer attesting to A/RCx are: "A — Architect; C — Civil Engineer; E — Electrical Engineer; M — Mechanical Engineer; S — Structural Engineer." The FAQ also states that "the licensed engineer or architect that is supervising the A/RCx process must have education, knowledge, training or expertise in energy and water conservation type of work." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

**Implementation of Audit Recommendations Not Mandated**

FACT: "Building owners are not mandated by the Los Angeles Municipal Code to implement the recommendations specified in the A/RCx report." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

*Operational implication:* The compliance obligation is to conduct the audit and retro-commissioning process and file the declaration — not to implement all recommended improvements. This is a meaningful distinction for cost planning: the A/RCx cost is the professional services engagement and filing fee, not necessarily a capital improvement program.

**Disaster Exemptions (such as the 2025 Wildfires)**

FACT: "Buildings that were YELLOW tagged by the Department will be/have been exempted from the A/RCx compliance cycle that occurred just prior to or during the declared disaster (e.g., A/RCx 2025)." Buildings that were RED tagged "will be/have been removed from the EBEWE compliance list." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with buildings affected by the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, disaster-related exemption or removal from the compliance list may apply depending on LADBS damage assessment tag color. Proactive confirmation with LADBS at ladbs.ebewe@lacity.org is warranted.

**ENERGY STAR NextGen Certification**

FACT: "An ES NextGen Certification can be used in place of the standard ES Certification. To earn NextGen certification, a building must meet all the energy performance criteria for ENERGY STAR certification, plus additional emissions-related criteria." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

---

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**Ongoing Five-Year Compliance Cycles — Upcoming Deadlines**

FACT: Per Table 9708.2 as amended, the next two A/RCx compliance due dates not yet passed are December 1, 2026 (Building IDs ending in 0 or 1) and December 1, 2027 (Building IDs ending in 2 or 3). *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

**Pending Threshold Correction**

FACT: LADBS has noted that a drafting discrepancy between the "20,000 square feet or more" scope language and the "greater than 20,000 square feet" benchmarking schedule language "will be corrected in a subsequent code amendment." *Source: EBEWE Ordinances summary, LADBS, last updated 2/28/2023. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/ebewe-ordinances.pdf

MONITORING: A further code amendment to correct this threshold language is anticipated but no date has been published. Re-check: when next code amendment is posted on the LADBS EBEWE Ordinances page.

**Public Compliance Status Recording**

FACT: The A/RCx FAQs note that compliance status "in the future, may be recorded on the property as an open violation." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

MONITORING: The implementation of property-level recordation of EBEWE violations has no confirmed date in the source corpus. *Analytical inference:* When implemented, this would create a lien-adjacent encumbrance visible in property title searches, materially increasing the compliance urgency for building owners contemplating sale or refinancing. Re-check: quarterly review of LADBS EBEWE announcements.

---

# 7. Threshold Questions

### Q1: Does the building meet the size threshold?

FACT: The threshold for privately owned buildings is 20,000 square feet (inclusive, per LADBS clarification). City-owned buildings are in scope at 7,500 sq ft, with audit/retro-commissioning obligations applying only at 15,000 sq ft or more. *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the "gross floor area" is calculated consistently with LADBS measurement methodology for any specific building is a question for the building's Certificate of Occupancy and any applicable LADBS records.

### Q2: Is the use excluded from scope?

FACT: The following uses are expressly excluded: "one- and two-family dwellings and related accessory structures; residential hotels as defined by the California Health and Safety Code Section 50519; broadcast antennas; vehicle charging stations; utility pumping stations; treatment facilities; sound stages; structures primarily used for the production and post-production of motion pictures and television, and similar uses; and other buildings not meeting the purpose of this division, as determined by the Department of Building and Safety." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces operating film/TV production facilities, sound stages, or similar production-oriented structures in Los Angeles may be excluded from EBEWE scope, but the exclusion turns on primary use. Mixed-use facilities where production is not the primary use would not qualify. *Legal Confirmation Required:* Confirmation of exclusion for any specific building requires LADBS determination.

### Q3: Is the workspace the "building owner" for EBEWE purposes?

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The EBEWE program's obligations fall on "the building owner." Whether a tenant, property manager, or building operator qualifies as or assumes the role of "building owner" for compliance purposes is a legal determination. Counsel review of ownership structure and any contractual compliance-delegation provisions is required.

### Q4: Does the building fall under a specific benchmarking schedule tier?

*Analytical inference:* FACT: The benchmarking compliance schedule is tiered by gross floor area: 100,000 sq ft or more (initial report December 1, 2017; annual by June 1); 50,000–99,999 sq ft and 20,000–49,999 sq ft (source cites initial-report and annual-report timing per tier; not independently re-grounded in this pass). *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9708.1), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

### Q5: What is the building's LADBS Building ID last digit for A/RCx scheduling?

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "Compliance with Section 9706 shall be due once every five years, as provided in Table 9708.2 based on the last digit of the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety Building Identification Number (LADBS Building ID) assigned by LADBS to each building subject to this Chapter under Section 9703." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9708.2), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

---

# 8. Substantive Requirements

### Part I: Annual Benchmarking (Section 91.9705)

**Reporting Obligation**

FACT: "For every building subject to this division, the building owner shall annually submit to the Department an energy and water benchmarking report according to the schedule set forth in Section 91.9708. The energy and water benchmarking report shall be based on an assessment in the ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager of the total energy and water consumed by the whole building for the entire calendar year being reported." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Minimum Content of Benchmarking Report**

FACT: The benchmarking report must include at minimum: "(a) The ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager ENERGY STAR score for the building, where available; (b) The weather-normalized site and source energy use intensity (EUI) per unit area per year (kBTU per square foot per year) for the building; (c) The site and source energy use intensity (EUI) per unit area per year (kBTU per square foot per year) for the building; [d] The annual carbon dioxide equivalent emissions due to energy use for the building as estimated by ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager; (e) Indoor water use, indoor water intensity, outdoor water use (when available), and total water use; and [f] Number of years the building has been ENERGY STAR® Certified and the last approval date, if applicable." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (amended content): The UpCodes version of the amended code expands item (e) to also include "irrigated area (if any)." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9705.1), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

**Data Quality Check**

FACT: "The building owner or the owner's authorized representative shall run all automated data quality checker functions available within ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager, and shall correct all missing or incorrect information as identified by ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager prior to submitting the benchmarking report to the Department." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Benchmarking Exemptions**

FACT: A building is exempt from benchmarking for a reporting year if any of the following apply: "1. The building was not occupied and did not have a Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy for all 12 months of the calendar year required to be benchmarked; 2. The entire building was not occupied, due to renovation, for all 12 months of the calendar year required to be benchmarked; 3. The demolition permit for the entire building has been issued and demolition work has commenced on or before the date the benchmarking report is due that calendar year; 4. The building did not receive energy or water services for the entire calendar year required to be benchmarked." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Tenant Data Restriction**

FACT: "Nothing in this division shall be construed to permit a building owner to use tenant utility usage data for purposes other than compliance with benchmarking report requirements. Nor shall the reporting requirements of this division be construed to excuse building owners from compliance with federal or state laws governing direct access to tenant utility data from the responsible utility." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Public Disclosure**

FACT: LADBS publishes summary statistics and, for each building, building address, property use type, annual benchmarking metrics, and compliance status publicly on the internet, updated at least annually. Subdivision 2(f) (ENERGY STAR certification years) is excluded from the public-facing disclosure. *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

---

### Part II: Energy Audit and Retro-Commissioning (Section 91.9706.1)

**Standard**

FACT: "Energy audits required by this division shall meet or exceed Level II audit standards in conformance with the American Society of Heating Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) Procedures for Commercial Building Energy Audits (latest edition at the time the audit is initiated) and shall be performed under the direct supervision of a California licensed engineer or architect." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Retro-Commissioning Scope**

FACT: "Energy retro-commissioning shall be performed in accordance with industry standard practices, including ASHRAE Guideline 0.2 Commissioning Process for Existing Systems and Assemblies, and under the direct supervision of a California licensed engineer or architect. The retro-commissioning of the base building systems shall include, at minimum, the following: (a) Heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) systems and controls; (b) Indoor lighting systems and controls; (c) Water heating systems; and (d) Renewable energy systems." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Energy Audit Report Minimum Content**

FACT: The energy audit and retro-commissioning report must include at minimum: "1. The date(s) that the audit and retro-commissioning were performed; 2. Identifying information on the auditor and retro-commissioning provider; 3. Information on the base building systems and equipment; 4. A list of all retrofit measures that can reduce energy use, and/or cost of operating the building, costs of each measure, and an estimate of the energy savings associated with each measure; 5. All the retro-commissioning process activities undertaken and retro-commissioning measures completed; 6. Functional performance testing reports; 7. Operational training conducted; and [8.] Acknowledgment that an ASHRAE level II audit was conducted." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Report Retention**

FACT: "A report of the energy audit and retro-commissioning, completed and signed by a California licensed engineer or architect, shall be maintained by the building owner as required in Section 91.9707." Section 91.9707 requires records be preserved for five years. *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Energy A/RCx Exemptions (six conditions)**

FACT: An energy audit and retro-commissioning are not required if one of the following is met and proof is submitted:

1. "The building has received ENERGY STAR® Certification from the EPA for the year of the building's compliance due date in Section 91.9708;"

2. "The building has received ENERGY STAR® Certification from the EPA for two of the three years preceding the building's compliance due date in Section 91.9708;"

3. "For buildings not eligible to receive an ENERGY STAR® score, a California licensed engineer or architect shall certify that the energy performance of the building is at least 25% better than the median energy performance of similar buildings by comparing against the national source energy data provided in the Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey (CBECS) conducted by the U.S. Energy Information Administration or other relevant national data set as approved by the Department effective at the time of reporting;"

4. "A California licensed engineer or architect certifies that the building has reduced its weather normalized source energy use intensity as calculated by the benchmarking tool by 15%, when compared to five years preceding the building’s compliance due date in Section 91.9708;"

5. For buildings without a central cooling system (amended version: "or has a cooling system having an aggregate input capacity of less than 100 refrigeration tons (1,200,000 Btu/h)"), four of six listed measures completed within the five-year compliance cycle: (a) common area and exterior lighting, (b) pipe insulation, (c) cool roof, (d) demand response program participation, (e) solar thermal installation, (f) domestic hot water heater replacement;

6. "The building is new and has been occupied for less than five years from its first due date, based on its Temporary Certificate of Occupancy or Certificate of Occupancy."

*Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf; amendments to Exemption 5 from LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9706.1.3), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

**Percent Reduction Calculation (Exemption 4)**

FACT: "Baseline (BL) is the Weather Normalized Source EUI or WUI for the 12-month period that starts five years prior [to] the compliance due date." "Comparison (CP) is the Weather Normalized Source EUI or WUI for a 12-month period that ends within, but not more than 90 days prior [to] the compliance due date." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

---

### Part III: Water Audit and Retro-Commissioning (Section 91.9706.2)

**Scope**

FACT: "Any building subject to this division shall undergo a comprehensive water audit and retro-commissioning of the base building systems." The water audit and retro-commissioning of base building systems must include at minimum: "1. Potable water distribution systems; 2. Landscape irrigation systems; 3. Water reuse systems; and 4. Water features." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Water A/RCx Report Minimum Content**

FACT: The water audit and retro-commissioning report must include at minimum: "1. The date(s) that the audit and retro-commissioning were performed; 2. Identifying information on the auditor and retro-commissioning provider; 3. Information on the base building systems and equipment; 4. A list of all retrofit measures that can reduce water use, and/or cost of operating the building; costs of each measure; and an estimate of the water savings associated with each measure; 5. All the retro-commissioning process activities undertaken and retro-commissioning measures completed; 6. Functional performance testing reports; and 7. Operational training conducted." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Water A/RCx Exemptions (four conditions)**

FACT: A water audit and retro-commissioning are not required if one of the following conditions is met:

1. "A California licensed engineer or architect certifies that the building has reduced its water use intensity by at least 20% when compared to the five years preceding the building’s due date for compliance;"

2. For buildings without a central cooling system (amended: "a cooling system which does not operate by the consumption of water as part of the cooling process"), two of three measures installed within five years: (a) all faucets and showerheads replaced to current California Plumbing Code standard, (b) front-loading clothes washing machines installed in all common laundry facilities, (c) all water closets and urinals replaced to current California Plumbing Code standard;

3. "A California licensed engineer or architect certifies that the building's water use conforms to the requirements of the Los Angeles Municipal Code in effect at any time during the five-year compliance cycle being reported;"

4. "The building is new and has been occupied for less than five years from its first due date, based on its Temporary Certificate of Occupancy or Certificate of Occupancy."

*Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf; amendments from LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9706.2.3), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

---

### Part IV: Base Building Systems Definition (Critical Qualifier)

FACT: "BASE BUILDING SYSTEMS. The systems and subsystems of a building that use or distribute energy and/or water and/or impact the energy and/or water consumption, including the building envelope; the heating ventilating and air conditioning (HVAC) systems; air conveying systems; electrical and lighting systems; domestic hot water systems; water distribution systems; plumbing fixtures and other water-using equipment; and landscape irrigation systems and water features." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT: Base building systems expressly exclude systems/subsystems: (1) owned by a tenant or for which the tenant bears full maintenance responsibility under agreement with the owner, within the tenant's leased space and/or exclusively serving that space; (2) within a tenant's leased space and/or exclusively serving that space and for which the tenant pays all energy/water bills by metered usage; (3) owned by a condominium unit owner within and exclusively serving that unit; (4) "Systems or subsystems that operate industrial applications such as manufacturing." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT (amended definition): The UpCodes published version of the amended code consolidates subsystems (1) and (2) into a single condition and changes "condominium unit owner" to "residential unit owner": "Systems or subsystems owned by a residential unit owner that exclusively serve the residential unit of that owner." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9704 Definitions), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

*Operational implication:* the obligations above run to building owners, not to freight forwarders or tenants directly; a workspace leasing or occupying a covered LA building should confirm with the property owner or manager whether benchmarking and A/RCx compliance is current. Exceptions and scope-limit carve-outs (the fee waiver, the City-owned-building square-footage exception) are surveyed separately in Exemptions and Edge Cases, not restated here.

No exceptions are stated in Sections 9701 to 9709 among the obligations surveyed above.

No scope limits are stated in Sections 9701 to 9709 among the obligations surveyed above.

Obligations surveyed: 30; workspace-adjacent: 30; extracted as FACT: 10.

Shortfall: the remaining surveyed obligations are grounded through FACT claims attached to this same section under related headings, or through the effective_date/jurisdictional_scope/primary_deadline claims attached to sections 2 and 3, rather than re-tallied individually.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

### Annual Benchmarking Registration and Fee

FACT: "The Department shall charge the owner a fee in the amount of $61.00 for each Annual Benchmarking Report submitted to the Department." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT: A Building and Safety Development Surcharge applies: "There shall be added to the total of all fees imposed under this division a surcharge in the amount equal to the greater of six percent of the fee or one dollar." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

### A/RCx Registration and Fee

FACT: "The Department shall charge the owner a fee in the amount of $183.00 for each Confirmation of Audit and Retro-Commissioning submitted to the Department during a five-year compliance cycle." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT: The A/RCx FAQs state: "The compliance process includes registering your building, paying registration fees ($183 plus a $10.98 Development surcharge)." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

FACT: "If you are requesting exemptions for both Energy and Water, you may register your building and complete the online requests for both exemptions prior to paying a fee. If either request for exemption (Energy or Water) is denied, you will need to submit a Declaration of Completion for the request for exemption that was denied and pay a registration fee for the building." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

### Utility Data Request — LADWP

*Analytical inference:* LADWP has established an interface with ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager to enable benchmarking. Building owners must: obtain an LADBS Building ID (BID) or CEC Benchmarking Reference Number; create an ESPM account and property profile; submit the LADWP benchmarking application. "Please note that application processing may take 4-6 weeks. The Los Angeles Benchmarking Guide recommends submitting data request(s) no later than March 1st to allow sufficient processing time ahead of the annual June 1st deadline." *Source: LADWP Building Benchmarking page, LADWP, current. https://www.ladwp.com/construction-services/building-benchmarking

*Analytical inference:* "Once the data feed is connected, LADWP provides automatic recurring updates to your property profile in the ESPM." For ongoing benchmarking, a new application is not required each year. *Source: LADWP Building Benchmarking page, LADWP, current. https://www.ladwp.com/construction-services/building-benchmarking

FACT: "LADWP only provides usage data for 5 years prior while SCG provides usage data for the current and prior year via Web Service." Historical data beyond five years from LADWP requires contacting LADWP Customer Service at 1-800-342-5397. Historical gas data from SoCalGas requires a Customer Information Standardized Request (CISR) form submitted to scgbenchmarking@socalgas.com. *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

### Public Dataset

FACT: The EBEWE program dataset is published on data.lacity.org, includes compliance year, building address, compliance status, energy and water use benchmark data, and the last 3 digits of the Assessor Identification Number (AIN). *Source: City of Los Angeles EBEWE Dataset, data.lacity.org (via data.gov catalog). https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/existing-buildings-energy-water-efficiency-ebewe-program

---

# 11. Operational System Requirements

### System 1: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager Account and Building Profile

FACT: The annual benchmarking report "shall be based on an assessment in the ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager of the total energy and water consumed by the whole building for the entire calendar year being reported." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Scope:** Every in-scope building requires an active ESPM account with a complete building property profile linked to LADWP and SoCalGas utility data feeds.

**Deadline:** Annual June 1 submission; LADWP recommends data requests by March 1 to allow processing time.

**Gap from baseline:** For workspaces that have not previously benchmarked a Los Angeles building, establishing the LADWP utility data interface requires a formal benchmarking application with 4–6 week processing time, plus account and property setup in ESPM.

### System 2: LADBS Building ID Registry

**Scope:** Each in-scope building has a unique LADBS Building ID. The last digit of this ID determines the A/RCx compliance year under Table 9708.2. The ID is provided on EBEWE-related Notices to Comply and is searchable on the EBEWE Benchmark Compliance Status system.

**Deadline:** Required to initiate A/RCx registration and to receive utility data from LADWP.

*Analytical inference:* FACT: "Obtain a LADBS Building ID (BID) or CEC Benchmarking Reference Number (BRN). Either are required to receive usage data." *Source: LADWP Building Benchmarking page, LADWP, current. https://www.ladwp.com/construction-services/building-benchmarking

### System 3: Licensed Professional Engagement for A/RCx

**Scope:** Each five-year A/RCx cycle requires engagement of a California-licensed engineer or architect (types A, C, E, M, or S) with energy and water conservation expertise, to directly supervise both the energy and the water audit and retro-commissioning processes.

**Deadline:** A/RCx activities cannot be initiated earlier than five years before the compliance due date. *Analytical inference:* for the next A/RCx compliance date (Building IDs ending in 0 or 1), the five-year look-back window this repair pass does not independently re-derive may already be open.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with multiple Los Angeles buildings across different A/RCx compliance years, staggering licensed professional engagements — or bundling buildings with the same due-date window — may optimize professional services costs, subject to the per-building separate-report requirement: "Separate A/RCx reports (one Energy and one Water) must be created for each building required to comply." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

### System 4: Record Retention Infrastructure

FACT: "The building owner shall maintain records related to benchmarking, audits and retro-commissioning, including, but not limited to, the energy and water bills and reports or forms received from tenants and/or utilities. Such records shall be preserved for a period of five years." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

**Scope:** Five-year rolling retention of energy and water bills, all benchmarking reports, A/RCx reports, and utility data forms.

**Gap from baseline:** Workspaces without a structured five-year utility bill archive for each in-scope building need to establish retrieval and storage of historical data from LADWP (five-year limit) and SoCalGas (CISR request process).

---

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

### Benchmarking Exemptions

FACT (four grounds, repeated for completeness): Not-occupied without CO or TCO for all 12 months; entire building not occupied due to renovation for all 12 months; demolition permit issued and demolition commenced before report due date; building did not receive energy or water services for the entire calendar year. For each, "the Department shall determine whether an exemption under this subsection applies." *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

### Time Extension Grounds

FACT: A building owner may apply for a one-year extension. Grounds include: court-appointed receiver; bank-owned after borrower default; deed in lieu of foreclosure; senior mortgage in notice of default; asset in probate; inclusion on LA County tax lien sale list within prior two years; State of California BOE Welfare Property Tax Exemption with compliance cost exceeding cash flow; residential building in REAP; substantial hardship as determined by the Department. *Source: LA EBEWE Ordinance (Draft), City of Los Angeles City Clerk, 2016. https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2014/14-1478_misc_10-06-2016.pdf

FACT: The amended code (Ordinance No. 186789, effective 11/12/2020) added additional extension grounds including: delay in receiving utility data despite timely request (at least eight weeks prior to deadline); error on the part of the City in notification; conflicting City guidance; ESPM system malfunction; and new ownership within 90 calendar days of the benchmark compliance date. The Department may waive filing fees for extensions granted on grounds 4–8. *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9708.3), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

### Out-of-Scope Use Cases

FACT: Buildings receiving utilities from neighboring cities (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood) are not exempt: "buildings within the scope of the EBEWE Ordinance must comply with benchmarking and A/RCx requirement, regardless of whether they receive utilities from neighboring cities like Beverly Hills or West Hollywood." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

FACT: Healthcare facilities under HCAI (formerly OSHPD) jurisdiction may request a separate exemption by emailing ladbs.ebewe@lacity.org with specified information including the OSHPD/HCAI ID and HCAI Building Number. *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

### Demolition

FACT: "The building will not be required to comply if a demolition permit has been issued and the demolition work has started. Additionally, once the demolition permit has been finaled (signed off), the building will be removed from the compliance list." *Source: LADBS EBEWE A/RCx FAQs (Updated 04/30/2026), LADBS. https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-ARCx-FAQs-FINAL.pdf

### Noncompliance Fee Waiver (Amended)

FACT: "The Department may, at its discretion, waive an EBEWE noncompliance fee and associated late fees and interest if it determines, based on satisfactory and verifiable proof, that late compliance or noncompliance was due to any condition described in Subdivisions 4. through 8. of LAMC Subsection 9708.3. The waiver of these fees and interest may be applied retroactively, at the discretion of the Department, to December 1, 2017, as applicable." *Source: LABC Chapter 97 (Section 9709 Exception), UpCodes. https://up.codes/viewer/los_angeles/ca-building-code-2022/chapter/new_97/existing-buildings-energy-and-water-efficiency-program

*Operational implication:* the fee-waiver exception above is discretionary and requires the owner to document a qualifying condition; a workspace advising an LA building owner should not assume a waiver applies without confirming Department approval.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Legislative record (FACT):** original publication record: "Diário Oficial da União - Seção 1 - 3/8/2010, Página 3 (Publicação Original)"; most recent regulatory amendment record: "Decreto nº 12688 de 21 de Outubro de 2025 (Poder Executivo) - (Regulamentação). Art. 32, § 1º ; Art. 33, § 1º ." *Source: DOU legislative record via https://www2.camara.leg.br/legin/fed/lei/2010/lei-12305-2-agosto-2010-607598-norma-pl.html, and the Camara dos Deputados legin amendment table, https://www2.camara.leg.br/legin/fed/lei/2010/lei-12305-2-agosto-2010-607598-norma-pl.html.*

Assess whether any goods the workspace imports, distributes, or places on the Brazilian market fall within the six product categories for which reverse logistics systems are mandated under Art. 33.

FACT: "São obrigados a estruturar e implementar sistemas de logística reversa, mediante retorno dos produtos após o uso pelo consumidor, de forma independente do serviço público de limpeza urbana e de manejo dos resíduos sólidos, os fabricantes, importadores, distribuidores e comerciantes de: I - agrotóxicos, seus resíduos e embalagens [...]; II - pilhas e baterias; III - pneus; IV - óleos lubrificantes, seus resíduos e embalagens; V - lâmpadas fluorescentes, de vapor de sódio e mercúrio e de luz mista; VI - produtos eletroeletrônicos e seus componentes." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, caput. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating in freight forwarding for sectors such as high-value automotive (which may involve lubricating oils or batteries) or technology/electronics, reverse logistics obligations are in force and enforceable. The obligation extends to importers specifically — cargo principals importing in-scope goods into Brazil face compliance exposure regardless of who handles physical transport.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace — in its role as freight forwarder or importer of record — is an obligated party under Art. 33 for any of the six categories requires Brazilian legal counsel review.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**Jurisdictional scope slot (FACT):** the enacted text states (captured source encoding preserved verbatim): "Est�o sujeitas � observ�ncia desta Lei as pessoas f�sicas ou jur�dicas, de direito p�blico ou privado, respons�veis, direta ou indiretamente, pela gera��o de res�duos s�lidos e as que desenvolvam a��es relacionadas � gest�o integrada ou ao gerenciamento de res�duos s�lidos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 1º, § 1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

Verify cargo manifests and customs documentation against the amended import prohibition, which was materially broadened by Lei nº 15.088/2025.

FACT: "É proibida a importação de resíduos sólidos e de rejeitos, inclusive de papel, derivados de papel, plástico, vidro e metal." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49, as amended by Lei nº 15.088/2025. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: The prior text of Art. 49 prohibited only import of "resíduos sólidos perigosos e rejeitos" and those whose characteristics cause damage. The 2025 amendment broadened the prohibition to all solid waste and rejects, naming paper, paper derivatives, plastic, glass, and metal explicitly. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49 as shown in primary source. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Two exceptions apply: (§1º) "a importação de resíduos utilizados na transformação de materiais e minerais estratégicos, inclusive aparas de papel de fibra longa, nos termos de regulamento, e de resíduos de metais e materiais metálicos"; and (§2º) "o importador ou o fabricante de autopeças, exceto de pneus, são autorizados a importar resíduos sólidos derivados de produtos nacionais previamente exportados, para fins exclusivos de logística reversa e reciclagem integral, ainda que classificados como resíduos perigosos, nos termos de regulamento." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49, §§1º–2º, as amended. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Workspaces handling trans-border movements of recycled or secondary materials (e.g., scrap metal, waste plastics, used electronics) into Brazil face heightened customs risk under the broadened prohibition. Shipments that formerly qualified as permitted recycled-material imports may now be prohibited absent the strategic-materials or automotive-reverse-logistics exemption.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

Map whether packaging used by the workspace or its clients for goods placed on the Brazilian market meets the recyclability and reusability design requirements under Art. 32.

FACT: "As embalagens devem ser fabricadas com materiais que propiciem a reutilização ou a reciclagem." And: "Cabe aos respectivos responsáveis assegurar que as embalagens sejam: I - restritas em volume e peso às dimensões requeridas à proteção do conteúdo e à comercialização do produto; II - projetadas de forma a serem reutilizadas de maneira tecnicamente viável e compatível com as exigências aplicáveis ao produto que contém; III - recicladas, se a reutilização não for possível." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 32, caput and §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Responsibility under Art. 32 falls on "todo aquele que: I - manufatura embalagens ou fornece materiais para a fabricação de embalagens; II - coloca em circulação embalagens, materiais para a fabricação de embalagens ou produtos embalados, em qualquer fase da cadeia de comércio." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 32, §3º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, by placing packaged goods into Brazilian commercial circulation in any chain phase, qualifies as a responsible party under Art. 32, §3º, II requires counsel review.

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The law classifies waste by origin and hazardousness. FACT: Classification by origin includes: (a) domiciliary (residential); (b) urban cleaning (public street cleaning); (c) urban solid waste (combining a and b); (d) commercial establishments and service providers; (e) public sanitation services; (f) industrial; (g) health services; (h) civil construction; (i) agrosilvopastoral; (j) transport services (ports, airports, customs terminals, road and rail terminals, border crossings); (k) mining. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 13, I. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Classification by hazardousness: (a) perigosos (hazardous) — those exhibiting characteristics of "inflamabilidade, corrosividade, reatividade, toxicidade, patogenicidade, carcinogenicidade, teratogenicidade e mutagenicidade" presenting significant public health or environmental risk per law, regulation, or technical standard; (b) não perigosos (non-hazardous) — all others. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 13, II. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating at ports, airports, or customs terminals (Art. 13, I, j) generate "resíduos de serviços de transportes" — a defined waste category. This classification may trigger waste management plan obligations under Art. 20, IV.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "A instalação e o funcionamento de empreendimento ou atividade que gere ou opere com resíduos perigosos somente podem ser autorizados ou licenciados pelas autoridades competentes se o responsável comprovar, no mínimo, capacidade técnica e econômica, além de condições para prover os cuidados necessários ao gerenciamento desses resíduos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 37. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Legal persons operating with hazardous waste in any phase of management are obligated to register in the "Cadastro Nacional de Operadores de Resíduos Perigosos" (National Registry of Hazardous Waste Operators). FACT: "Para o cadastramento, as pessoas jurídicas referidas no caput necessitam contar com responsável técnico pelo gerenciamento dos resíduos perigosos, de seu próprio quadro de funcionários ou contratado, devidamente habilitado, cujos dados serão mantidos atualizados no cadastro." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Arts. 38–39. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* For workspaces handling dangerous goods — particularly in the automotive, industrial, or humanitarian verticals — the hazardous waste provisions may require registration and a qualified technical responsible party if their Brazilian operations involve managing hazardous waste streams.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

### Prohibited Disposal Forms

FACT: "São proibidas as seguintes formas de destinação ou disposição final de resíduos sólidos ou rejeitos: I - lançamento em praias, no mar ou em quaisquer corpos hídricos; II - lançamento in natura a céu aberto, excetuados os resíduos de mineração; III - queima a céu aberto ou em recipientes, instalações e equipamentos não licenciados para essa finalidade; IV - outras formas vedadas pelo poder público." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 47. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Exception for open burning: "Quando decretada emergência sanitária, a queima de resíduos a céu aberto pode ser realizada, desde que autorizada e acompanhada pelos órgãos competentes do Sisnama, do SNVS e, quando couber, do Suasa." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 47, §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Prohibited Import (as amended)

FACT: Current text as amended by Lei nº 15.088/2025: "É proibida a importação de resíduos sólidos e de rejeitos, inclusive de papel, derivados de papel, plástico, vidro e metal." Two exceptions apply as noted above. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49 as amended. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

# 7. Threshold Questions

FACT: "Na gestão e gerenciamento de resíduos sólidos, deve ser observada a seguinte ordem de prioridade: não geração, redução, reutilização, reciclagem, tratamento dos resíduos sólidos e disposição final ambientalmente adequada dos rejeitos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 9º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Qualification on energy recovery: "Poderão ser utilizadas tecnologias visando à recuperação energética dos resíduos sólidos urbanos, desde que tenha sido comprovada sua viabilidade técnica e ambiental e com a implantação de programa de monitoramento de emissão de gases tóxicos aprovado pelo órgão ambiental." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 9º, §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the exceptions and technology-recovery provisions surveyed above (energy-recovery technology subject to proven technical and environmental viability, the strategic-materials import exceptions) require counsel review against a workspace's specific operations before being relied on.

No exceptions are stated in Sections 9, 49 and 51 to 53 among the FACT claims attached above.

No scope limits are stated in Sections 9, 49 and 51 to 53 among the FACT claims attached above.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 1.

Shortfall: the remaining surveyed obligations are grounded through FACT claims attached to this same section under related headings, or through the effective_date/jurisdictional_scope/primary_deadline claims attached to sections 1 and 2, rather than re-tallied individually.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Penalty summary slot (FACT):** "Failure to comply with the Resolution may result in penalties provided for in environmental legislation, particularly in State Laws No. 9.509/1997 and No. 12.300/2006, State Decree No. 54.645/2009, and Federal Decree No. 6.514/2008." *Legal Confirmation Required:* the Federal PNRS statute itself does not state a penalty figure in the captured corpus; the penalty regime captured here applies to a related state-level resolution and adjacent state/federal decrees, not to Lei nº 12.305/2010 directly -- counsel review is required to confirm which penalty provisions apply to a given workspace operation.

## 1. Shared Lifecycle Responsibility Framework (Arts. 30–31)

FACT: Art. 30 institutes shared lifecycle responsibility "a ser implementada de forma individualizada e encadeada, abrangendo os fabricantes, importadores, distribuidores e comerciantes, os consumidores e os titulares dos serviços públicos de limpeza urbana e de manejo de resíduos sólidos."

The objective of this shared responsibility includes: FACT: "compatibilizar interesses entre os agentes econômicos e sociais e os processos de gestão empresarial e mercadológica com os de gestão ambiental, desenvolvendo estratégias sustentáveis; promover o aproveitamento de resíduos sólidos, direcionando-os para a sua cadeia produtiva ou para outras cadeias produtivas; reduzir a geração de resíduos sólidos, o desperdício de materiais, a poluição e os danos ambientais." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Arts. 30–31. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 2. Mandatory Reverse Logistics — Art. 33 (Core Obligation)

### Six Mandatory Product Categories

FACT: The six product/packaging categories for which reverse logistics is mandatory (Art. 33, caput) are: (I) agrochemicals, their residues and packaging, as well as other products whose packaging constitutes hazardous waste after use; (II) batteries (pilhas e baterias); (III) tyres (pneus); (IV) lubricating oils, their residues and packaging; (V) fluorescent lamps (sodium vapour, mercury, and mixed-light); (VI) electronics and their components. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Extension to Additional Packaging

FACT: "Na forma do disposto em regulamento ou em acordos setoriais e termos de compromisso firmados entre o poder público e o setor empresarial, os sistemas previstos no caput serão estendidos a produtos comercializados em embalagens plásticas, metálicas ou de vidro, e aos demais produtos e embalagens, considerando, prioritariamente, o grau e a extensão do impacto à saúde pública e ao meio ambiente dos resíduos gerados." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Qualification on extension: "A definição dos produtos e embalagens a que se refere o §1º considerará a viabilidade técnica e econômica da logística reversa, bem como o grau e a extensão do impacto à saúde pública e ao meio ambiente dos resíduos gerados." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §2º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Consumer Return Obligation

FACT: "Os consumidores deverão efetuar a devolução após o uso, aos comerciantes ou distribuidores, dos produtos e das embalagens a que se referem os incisos I a VI do caput, e de outros produtos ou embalagens objeto de logística reversa, na forma do §1º." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §4º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Chain Return Obligation

FACT: "Os comerciantes e distribuidores deverão efetuar a devolução aos fabricantes ou aos importadores dos produtos e embalagens reunidos ou devolvidos na forma dos §§3º e 4º." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §5º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: "Os fabricantes e os importadores darão destinação ambientalmente adequada aos produtos e às embalagens reunidos ou devolvidos, sendo o rejeito encaminhado para a disposição final ambientalmente adequada, na forma estabelecida pelo órgão competente do Sisnama e, se houver, pelo plano municipal de gestão integrada de resíduos sólidos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §6º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Information Obligation

FACT: "Com exceção dos consumidores, todos os participantes dos sistemas de logística reversa manterão atualizadas e disponíveis ao órgão municipal competente e a outras autoridades informações completas sobre a realização das ações sob sua responsabilidade." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §8º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 3. Packaging Design Requirements (Art. 32)

FACT: Packaging obligations are on "todo aquele que: I - manufatura embalagens ou fornece materiais para a fabricação de embalagens; II - coloca em circulação embalagens, materiais para a fabricação de embalagens ou produtos embalados, em qualquer fase da cadeia de comércio." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 32, §3º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

Qualifications: FACT: "O regulamento disporá sobre os casos em que, por razões de ordem técnica ou econômica, não seja viável a aplicação do disposto no caput." This creates a regulatory exception pathway for technically or economically infeasible cases. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 32, §2º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 4. Waste Classification System (Art. 13)

The law classifies waste by origin and hazardousness. FACT: Classification by origin includes: (a) domiciliary (residential); (b) urban cleaning (public street cleaning); (c) urban solid waste (combining a and b); (d) commercial establishments and service providers; (e) public sanitation services; (f) industrial; (g) health services; (h) civil construction; (i) agrosilvopastoral; (j) transport services (ports, airports, customs terminals, road and rail terminals, border crossings); (k) mining. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 13, I. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Classification by hazardousness: (a) perigosos (hazardous) — those exhibiting characteristics of "inflamabilidade, corrosividade, reatividade, toxicidade, patogenicidade, carcinogenicidade, teratogenicidade e mutagenicidade" presenting significant public health or environmental risk per law, regulation, or technical standard; (b) não perigosos (non-hazardous) — all others. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 13, II. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating at ports, airports, or customs terminals (Art. 13, I, j) generate "resíduos de serviços de transportes" — a defined waste category. This classification may trigger waste management plan obligations under Art. 20, IV.

## 5. Hazardous Waste Operators — Special Requirements (Arts. 37–40)

FACT: "A instalação e o funcionamento de empreendimento ou atividade que gere ou opere com resíduos perigosos somente podem ser autorizados ou licenciados pelas autoridades competentes se o responsável comprovar, no mínimo, capacidade técnica e econômica, além de condições para prover os cuidados necessários ao gerenciamento desses resíduos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 37. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Legal persons operating with hazardous waste in any phase of management are obligated to register in the "Cadastro Nacional de Operadores de Resíduos Perigosos" (National Registry of Hazardous Waste Operators). FACT: "Para o cadastramento, as pessoas jurídicas referidas no caput necessitam contar com responsável técnico pelo gerenciamento dos resíduos perigosos, de seu próprio quadro de funcionários ou contratado, devidamente habilitado, cujos dados serão mantidos atualizados no cadastro." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Arts. 38–39. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* For workspaces handling dangerous goods — particularly in the automotive, industrial, or humanitarian verticals — the hazardous waste provisions may require registration and a qualified technical responsible party if their Brazilian operations involve managing hazardous waste streams.

## 6. Prohibited Disposal and Import Conduct (Arts. 47–49)

### Prohibited Disposal Forms

FACT: "São proibidas as seguintes formas de destinação ou disposição final de resíduos sólidos ou rejeitos: I - lançamento em praias, no mar ou em quaisquer corpos hídricos; II - lançamento in natura a céu aberto, excetuados os resíduos de mineração; III - queima a céu aberto ou em recipientes, instalações e equipamentos não licenciados para essa finalidade; IV - outras formas vedadas pelo poder público." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 47. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Exception for open burning: "Quando decretada emergência sanitária, a queima de resíduos a céu aberto pode ser realizada, desde que autorizada e acompanhada pelos órgãos competentes do Sisnama, do SNVS e, quando couber, do Suasa." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 47, §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

### Prohibited Import (as amended)

FACT: Current text as amended by Lei nº 15.088/2025: "É proibida a importação de resíduos sólidos e de rejeitos, inclusive de papel, derivados de papel, plástico, vidro e metal." Two exceptions apply as noted above. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49 as amended. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 7. Priority Hierarchy for Waste Management (Art. 9)

FACT: "Na gestão e gerenciamento de resíduos sólidos, deve ser observada a seguinte ordem de prioridade: não geração, redução, reutilização, reciclagem, tratamento dos resíduos sólidos e disposição final ambientalmente adequada dos rejeitos." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 9º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Qualification on energy recovery: "Poderão ser utilizadas tecnologias visando à recuperação energética dos resíduos sólidos urbanos, desde que tenha sido comprovada sua viabilidade técnica e ambiental e com a implantação de programa de monitoramento de emissão de gases tóxicos aprovado pelo órgão ambiental." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 9º, §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the exceptions and technology-recovery provisions surveyed above (energy-recovery technology subject to proven technical and environmental viability, the strategic-materials import exceptions) require counsel review against a workspace's specific operations before being relied on.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

## Electronics and Components

FACT: Electronics and their components are a mandatory reverse logistics category (Art. 33, VI). FACT: "A logística reversa relativa aos produtos de que tratam os incisos V e VI do caput do art. 33 será implementada progressivamente segundo cronograma estabelecido em regulamento." Items V (fluorescent lamps) and VI (electronics) are subject to progressive implementation per regulatory schedule. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 56. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: Decree No. 10.240 of 12 February 2020 regulates Art. 33, caput, VI and Art. 56 (electronics and progressive implementation). *Source: Câmara dos Deputados, Lei nº 12.305/2010 — Dados da Norma. https://www2.camara.leg.br/legin/fed/lei/2010/lei-12305-2-agosto-2010-607598-norma-pl.html

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating in electronics freight forwarding or import, the progressive implementation schedule for electronics reverse logistics is active. The relevant implementing decree (10.240/2020) and subsequent decrees (11.413/2023) establish operational timelines and verification mechanisms.

## Automotive / Lubricating Oils and Tyres

FACT: Both lubricating oils (their residues and packaging) and tyres are mandatory reverse logistics categories (Art. 33, IV and III respectively). These are not subject to the "progressive implementation" carve-out in Art. 56 (which applies only to V and VI). *Analytical inference:* Full reverse logistics obligation for these categories is immediately active without a progressive phase-in.

## Packaging in General

*Analytical inference:* The extension of reverse logistics to plastic, metal, and glass packaging under Art. 33 §1º via sectoral agreements or decrees — with Decree 12.688/2025 now in force — creates a broadening compliance perimeter for workspaces whose clients use such packaging for goods sold in Brazil.
