# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## 1. Hazardous Waste Operator Registry

FACT: "As pessoas jurídicas que operam com resíduos perigosos, em qualquer fase do seu gerenciamento, são obrigadas a se cadastrar no Cadastro Nacional de Operadores de Resíduos Perigosos." FACT: "O cadastro previsto no caput será coordenado pelo órgão federal competente do Sisnama e implantado de forma conjunta pelas autoridades federais, estaduais e municipais." FACT: "O cadastro a que se refere o caput é parte integrante do Cadastro Técnico Federal de Atividades Potencialmente Poluidoras ou Utilizadoras de Recursos Ambientais e do Sistema de Informações previsto no art. 12." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 38. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace's Brazilian operations involve hazardous waste management in any phase — including transit handling, consolidation, or storage of goods classified as hazardous — triggering mandatory registry requires counsel review.

## 2. Annual Reporting by Hazardous Waste Operators

FACT: Legal persons operating with hazardous waste are required to: "informar anualmente ao órgão competente do Sisnama e, se couber, do SNVS, sobre a quantidade, a natureza e a destinação temporária ou final dos resíduos sob sua responsabilidade." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 39, §2º, II. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 3. Waste Management Plan Reporting System

FACT: "Os responsáveis por plano de gerenciamento de resíduos sólidos manterão atualizadas e disponíveis ao órgão municipal competente, ao órgão licenciador do Sisnama e a outras autoridades, informações completas sobre a implementação e a operacionalização do plano sob sua responsabilidade." FACT: "Para a consecução do disposto no caput, sem prejuízo de outras exigências cabíveis por parte das autoridades, será implementado sistema declaratório com periodicidade, no mínimo, anual, na forma do regulamento." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 23, caput and §1º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 4. SINIR — National Solid Waste Information System

FACT: "A União, os Estados, o Distrito Federal e os Municípios organizarão e manterão, de forma conjunta, o Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre a Gestão dos Resíduos Sólidos (Sinir), articulado com o Sinisa e o Sinima." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 12. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Private sector participants in reverse logistics systems are required to report via SINIR. The MTR (waste transport manifesto) introduced by Decree 10.936/2022 feeds into SINIR, creating a traceability obligation for waste transport.

## 5. Reverse Logistics Participant Reporting

FACT: "Com exceção dos consumidores, todos os participantes dos sistemas de logística reversa manterão atualizadas e disponíveis ao órgão municipal competente e a outras autoridades informações completas sobre a realização das ações sob sua responsabilidade." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §8º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## 1. Waste Management Plan — Content and Technical Responsible Party

FACT: For entities subject to Art. 20, the waste management plan must contain as minimum: description of the operation; diagnosis of solid waste generated (origin, volume, characterization, environmental liabilities); identification of responsible parties per waste management stage; definition of operational procedures; identification of shared/consortium solutions; preventive and corrective actions for mismanagement accidents; targets for minimization, reuse, and recycling; measures addressing environmental liabilities; periodic revision schedule. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 21. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: "Para a elaboração, implementação, operacionalização e monitoramento de todas as etapas do plano de gerenciamento de resíduos sólidos, nelas incluído o controle da disposição final ambientalmente adequada dos rejeitos, será designado responsável técnico devidamente habilitado." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 22. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating Brazilian facilities (warehouses, freight terminals) that generate non-domestic-equivalent or hazardous waste must designate a qualified technical responsible party. This requires identifying a duly qualified person — from in-house staff or external contract — before the plan is submitted.

## 2. Reverse Logistics System Infrastructure

FACT: Art. 33 §3º specifies that obligated parties may, among other measures: "I - implantar procedimentos de compra de produtos ou embalagens usados; II - disponibilizar postos de entrega de resíduos reutilizáveis e recicláveis; III - atuar em parceria com cooperativas ou outras formas de associação de catadores de materiais reutilizáveis e recicláveis, nos casos de que trata o §1º." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 33, §3º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Workspaces assisting clients in structuring reverse logistics compliance can position themselves as logistics partners for the collection, transport, and return of in-scope products — a commercial opportunity alongside the compliance obligation.

## 3. Reverse Logistics Credit Mechanism

FACT: BVRio, in collaboration with the National Association of Catadores, developed in 2012 a Reverse Logistics Credits Mechanism to assist companies to meet their obligations under the law while rewarding Catadores for their role. FACT: "Reverse Logistics Credits are certificates that confirm that reverse logistics services were provided to ensure that a certain amount of waste was responsibly disposed of. These credits are issued and sold by cooperatives of Catadores and purchased by producers and/or importers who need to comply with the solid waste legislation." *Source: Circular Action Hub, Brazilian Solid Waste Legislation. https://www.circularactionhub.org/certification/brazilian-solid-waste-legislation/

*Operational implication:* For clients facing reverse logistics obligations, the credit mechanism provides a compliance pathway without requiring direct investment in collection infrastructure. Workspaces advising clients on Brazilian market entry can flag this mechanism as an operational alternative.

## 4. Waste Transport Manifesto (MTR)

FACT: Decree No. 10.936/2022 introduced the MTR as "a self-declared document valid throughout the national territory, aimed at ensuring the environmental monitoring of Reverse Logistics Systems." *Source: Mondaq/KLA Advogados, Reverse Logistics: Regulatory Decrees And The Role Of The States, 4 October 2024. https://www.mondaq.com/brazil/waste-management/1526446/reverse-logistics-regulatory-decrees-and-the-role-of-the-states

*Operational implication:* Any workspace arranging transport of solid waste, recyclable materials, or post-consumer returns within Brazil requires MTR documentation per Decree 10.936/2022. This is an operational system requirement for any Brazilian domestic logistics involving waste streams.

## 5. Hazardous Waste: Insurance and Technical Capacity

FACT: "No licenciamento ambiental de empreendimentos ou atividades que operem com resíduos perigosos, o órgão licenciador do Sisnama pode exigir a contratação de seguro de responsabilidade civil por danos causados ao meio ambiente ou à saúde pública, observadas as regras sobre cobertura e os limites máximos de contratação fixados em regulamento." Qualification: "O disposto no caput considerará o porte da empresa, conforme regulamento." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 40. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## 1. Radioactive Waste Exclusion

FACT: "Esta Lei não se aplica aos rejeitos radioativos, que são regulados por legislação específica." Complete exclusion — no PNRS obligations attach to radioactive waste. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 1º, §2º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 2. Mining Waste — Open-Air Disposal Exception

FACT: Art. 47, II prohibits open-air disposal "excetuados os resíduos de mineração" — mining waste is explicitly carved out from the open-air disposal prohibition. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 47, II. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 3. Commercial Waste Equiparated to Domiciliary Waste

FACT: "Respeitado o disposto no art. 20, os resíduos referidos na alínea 'd' do inciso I do caput [commercial establishment waste], se caracterizados como não perigosos, podem, em razão de sua natureza, composição ou volume, ser equiparados aos resíduos domiciliares pelo poder público municipal." Qualification: this applies only if characterised as non-hazardous and only by municipal authority decision. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 13, parágrafo único. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* If a workspace's Brazilian office or small operations generate non-hazardous commercial waste, there may be a pathway for municipal equiparation to domiciliary waste, reducing compliance burden. This is determined by municipal authority.

## 4. Simplified Waste Management Plan for Micro and Small Enterprises

FACT: "Serão estabelecidos em regulamento: [...] II - critérios e procedimentos simplificados para apresentação dos planos de gerenciamento de resíduos sólidos para microempresas e empresas de pequeno porte, assim consideradas as definidas nos incisos I e II do art. 3º da Lei Complementar nº 123, de 14 de dezembro de 2006, desde que as atividades por elas desenvolvidas não gerem resíduos perigosos." Qualification: the simplified procedure is not available if the enterprise generates hazardous waste. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 21, §3º, II. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 5. Art. 49 Import Prohibition — Two Statutory Exceptions

As noted above: (1) strategic materials and long-fibre paper offcuts per regulatory definition; (2) auto parts importers/manufacturers for products previously exported from Brazil, for exclusive reverse logistics and integral recycling purposes. *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 49, §§1º–2º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

## 6. Sectoral Agreements and Terms of Commitment

FACT: Sectoral agreements and terms of commitment can have national, regional, state, or municipal scope. FACT: "Os acordos setoriais e termos de compromisso firmados em âmbito nacional têm prevalência sobre os firmados em âmbito regional ou estadual, e estes sobre os firmados em âmbito municipal." FACT: "Na aplicação de regras concorrentes consoante o §1º, os acordos firmados com menor abrangência geográfica podem ampliar, mas não abrandar, as medidas de proteção ambiental constantes nos acordos setoriais e termos de compromisso firmados com maior abrangência geográfica." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 34, §§1º–2º. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Operational implication:* Where a client sector has a national-level sectoral agreement, that agreement governs reverse logistics obligations in that sector regardless of state law — unless the state law is more stringent. Workspaces advising clients must identify the applicable sectoral agreement tier.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## Extended Producer Responsibility Frameworks

FACT: The PNRS "paved the road for the development of Extended Producer Responsibility schemes in the country, as it establishes shared responsibility for the product life cycle (Art. 30) and determines the obligation of reverse logistics for generating companies (Article 33)." *Source: Circular Action Hub, Brazilian Solid Waste Legislation. https://www.circularactionhub.org/certification/brazilian-solid-waste-legislation/

## Waste Picker Integration as Compliance Pathway

FACT: "There are close to one million catadores in the country, many of which organized into hundreds of co-operatives and associations. While in the past, the remuneration of catadores was derived only from the sale of the recyclable materials collected, the PNRS established the basis for the remuneration for the environmental services of reverse logistics." *Source: Circular Action Hub, Brazilian Solid Waste Legislation. https://www.circularactionhub.org/certification/brazilian-solid-waste-legislation/

*Industry interpretation:* The catador cooperative system is a recognised, regulator-endorsed compliance mechanism. Workspaces with clients facing reverse logistics obligations — particularly for packaging, electronics, or consumer goods — can point to Reverse Logistics Credit purchases from catador cooperatives as both a compliance tool and a social value proposition in client communications.

## Academic Research on PNRS Implementation

FACT: A peer-reviewed study (Trigo et al., 2023) in the *Latin American Journal of Management for Sustainable Development* analysed Decree 10.936/2022 and found the principal results include "the evaluation of potential gains of scale and use of synergies of reverse logistics systems, respecting the effectiveness of the national information system on solid waste management for management continuous improvement" and noted that "the social contribution is the effective closure of all dumps and controlled landfills." *Source: Inderscience, Latin American Journal of Management for Sustainable Development, Vol.6 No.1, 2023. https://www.inderscience.com/info/inarticle.php?artid=132353

*Analytical inference:* Academic evidence suggests the Decree 10.936/2022 framework has scale-efficiency gains as a design objective — meaning compliance through collective/consortium reverse logistics arrangements (rather than individual systems) is both legally permitted and policy-encouraged. This is commercially relevant for workspaces proposing shared logistics solutions to clients.

## Circular Economy Integration

FACT: The PNRS "helps understand the impacts of the production process, not only in the use of raw materials, but also at the end of the life cycle for products consumed in the market. With instruments that establish a hierarchy of activities and priority for the prevention and reduction of waste generation, it promotes the concept of circular design." *Source: Enel Américas, Regulations on the National Solid Waste Policy (PNRS), 11 February 2022. https://www.enelamericas.com/en/circular-economy-latam/articles/regulations-on-the-national-solid-waste-policy-PNRS-and-creation-of-the-national-inverse-logistics-program.html

## Penalty Summary

FACT: "Sem prejuízo da obrigação de, independentemente da existência de culpa, reparar os danos causados, a ação ou omissão das pessoas físicas ou jurídicas que importe inobservância aos preceitos desta Lei ou de seu regulamento sujeita os infratores às sanções previstas em lei, em especial às fixadas na Lei nº 9.605, de 12 de fevereiro de 1998, que 'dispõe sobre as sanções penais e administrativas derivadas de condutas e atividades lesivas ao meio ambiente, e dá outras providências', e em seu regulamento." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 51. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: The law specifically amended Lei nº 9.605/1998, Art. 56 §1º, adding criminal liability for those who "manipula, acondiciona, armazena, coleta, transporta, reutiliza, recicla ou dá destinação final a resíduos perigosos de forma diversa da estabelecida em lei ou regulamento." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 53. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

FACT: "A observância do disposto no caput do art. 23 e no §2º do art. 39 desta Lei é considerada obrigação de relevante interesse ambiental para efeitos do art. 68 da Lei nº 9.605, de 1998, sem prejuízo da aplicação de outras sanções cabíveis nas esferas penal e administrativa." *Source: Lei nº 12.305/2010, Art. 52. https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2010/lei/l12305.htm

*Analytical inference:* The PNRS does not set out a standalone penalty tariff — it cross-references Brazil's Environmental Crimes Law (Lei 9.605/1998), which provides both administrative fines and criminal sanctions. Specific fine amounts under Lei 9.605 and its implementing decree (Decreto 6.514/2008) are not within the corpus sourced content.

Specific penalty quantum (fine amounts): *Specific administrative fine amounts not available from primary PNRS sources as of this brief's date. Amounts are governed by Lei nº 9.605/1998 and Decreto nº 6.514/2008 — Brazilian environmental counsel should confirm applicable sanctions.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers the July 6, 2026, final rule amending 40 CFR Part 63, Subpart DDDD — the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) for the Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) source category. The rule establishes new maximum achievable control technology (MACT) emission limitations and work practices for previously unregulated hazardous air pollutants (HAP) across PCWP process units and lumber kilns at major sources.

This document is structured as a regulatory fact document. All claims labeled **FACT** are span-grounded in the source corpus. Claims labeled *Analytical inference:*, *Industry interpretation:*, or *Operational implication:* are interpretive. Items requiring legal determination carry a *Legal Confirmation Required:* callout.

This brief covers the workspace in its role as a freight-forwarding and logistics operation serving shippers and facilities whose cargo may include materials processed at PCWP facilities — specifically as a potential compliance-chain participant for facilities that now face new emission and operational requirements that shape production schedules, kiln operating parameters, and facility-level costs. Workspaces handling lumber, engineered wood products, or composite panels — or operating in proximity to producers of these goods — should note that the rule's cost and operational requirements will ripple through production pricing and throughput timing.

**Convention note:** Compliance deadlines run on two tracks — new or reconstructed sources (effective July 6, 2026, or upon startup) and existing sources (compliance by the applicable existing-source deadline). Both tracks are referenced throughout.

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**Effective date slot (FACT):** "This final rule is effective on July 6, 2026." *Source: EPA Final Rule, Federal Register, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Penalty summary slot (FACT):** "A deviation is not always a violation. The determination of whether a deviation constitutes a violation of the standard is up to the discretion of the entity responsible for enforcement of the standards." *Source: 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, eCFR. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**Jurisdictional scope slot (FACT):** the definition of fiberboard mat dryer "applies to dryers in the wet/dry hardboard process." *Source: EPA Final Rule, Federal Register, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Effective date and jurisdictional scope — FACT:** "This final rule is effective on July 6, 2026." The rule applies to PCWP manufacturing facilities — defined in the regulation as major sources of HAP emissions — located in the United States and subject to 40 CFR Part 63, Subpart DDDD. *Source: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Plywood and Composite Wood Products, Final Rule, EPA/Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**What constitutes a major source — FACT:** The regulation defines major source as "a plant site that emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more, or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year from all emission sources at the plant site." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**What the rule does — FACT:** "The EPA is finalizing maximum achievable control technology (MACT) standards in the form of emission limitations and work practices as appropriate for total hazardous air pollutants (HAP) (including acetaldehyde, acrolein, formaldehyde, methanol, phenol, propionaldehyde), non-mercury (non-Hg) HAP metals, mercury (Hg), hydrogen chloride (HCl), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), dioxin/furan (D/F), and methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI). Sources affected by the amendments include PCWP process units and lumber kilns located at facilities that are major sources of HAP emissions." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Background and legal basis — FACT:** "These final amendments address the 2007 partial remand and vacatur of the 2004 final rule that promulgated the PCWP NESHAP ('2004 rule'). The final amendments also respond to issues raised in a petition for reconsideration regarding the 2020 residual risk and technology review (RTR) and other amendments to the 2020 PCWP NESHAP." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Current affected-facility count — FACT:** "There are currently 219 major source facilities that are subject to the PCWP NESHAP, including 93 facilities manufacturing PCWP and 126 facilities producing kiln-dried lumber." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Why this applies to the workspace:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces providing logistics or freight-forwarding services for facilities producing kiln-dried lumber, oriented strandboard (OSB), medium density fiberboard (MDF), plywood, or engineered wood products operate upstream and downstream of facilities now subject to new emission controls, production-monitoring mandates, kiln operating constraints, and performance-testing schedules. These facility-level requirements can affect production throughput, scheduling windows, and cost-per-unit — each of which has downstream effects on shipment volumes, tender timing, and commercial relationships. Workspaces in commodity lumber corridors should treat this rule as a production-environment signal.

---

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**Key date (FACT):** the site-specific plan deadline is "by January 6, 2028." *Source: EPA Final Rule, Federal Register, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Key dates (FACT):** existing-source compliance is due "by July 6, 2029"; the new-source applicability cutoff is "May 18, 2023." *Source: EPA Final Rule, Federal Register, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**Primary deadline slot (FACT):** the rule revises the rule to allow inspections to occur "no later than 13 months after the previous inspection." *Source: EPA Final Rule, Federal Register, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**ACTION REQUIRED — Assess supply-chain exposure to PCWP facility compliance timelines**

Assess whether the workspace's active shippers include facilities classified as existing PCWP major sources subject to the applicable existing-source compliance deadline. *Operational implication:* Existing PCWP facilities face a three-year capital and operational transition (new emission controls, monitoring equipment, performance testing, modified kiln operations) that may affect production scheduling, throughput, or facility-level costs — and in turn shipment volumes and booking predictability on affected lanes.

*Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**ACTION REQUIRED — Verify new-source compliance status for any PCWP construction commenced after the 2023 proposal date**

For any shipper or facility counterpart whose PCWP construction or reconstruction commenced after May 18, 2023: *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether that facility is classified as a "new affected source" under 40 CFR 63.2233(e)(1), which would require compliance with new standards beginning July 6, 2026, or upon initial startup, whichever is later — not the 2029 deadline that applies to existing sources.

*Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, effective July 6, 2026. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**COST ALERT — Flag annualized compliance cost exposure across shipper relationships**

Map commercial relationships with PCWP facilities against the EPA's published cost estimate. FACT: "The EPA estimates that this final action would cost approximately $121 million in total capital costs (distributed across multiple years) and $53 million per year (in 2024 dollars) in total annualized costs" across 219 existing and six projected new major source facilities. *Operational implication:* *Analytical inference:* per-facility annualized compliance costs vary by facility; the figures facilities will seek to recover through product pricing, potentially affecting the commodity pricing environment for lumber and wood panel products on lanes the workspace serves.

*Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**MONITORING — Track lumber kiln site-specific plan submission deadline**

Note the site-specific-plan deadline for lumber kilns choosing the site-specific plan work practice option. FACT: "The site-specific plan must be developed and submitted to the delegated authority by the applicable site-specific-plan deadline." *Operational implication:* Facilities still developing site-specific plans may defer certain operational decisions until 2028, creating a period of operational uncertainty affecting production scheduling on lumber lanes. Set a re-check window at Q3 2027.

*Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2253(b)(1). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The PCWP NESHAP regulatory obligations attach directly to facility owners and operators of PCWP manufacturing major sources. The workspace, in its freight-forwarding role, is not the compliance obligant under this regulation.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace entity that provides services at or to PCWP-regulated facilities — including on-site logistics operations, packaging fabrication on behalf of PCWP producers, or fulfillment functions physically located at major-source facilities — bears any secondary compliance exposure under state or local permit conditions that incorporate federal NESHAP requirements by reference.

*Analytical inference:* The practical compliance-chain relevance for workspaces in freight-forwarding roles is indirect: the regulation governs facility-level emissions and operations, but its operational requirements (kiln temperature limits, annual burner tune-ups, performance testing every five years, bypass stack monitoring, and O&M plan maintenance) constrain when and how facilities can operate, which in turn shapes production volume predictability and shipment patterns for cargo verticals that include lumber, OSB, MDF, plywood, engineered wood products, and glue-laminated beams.

**FACT — NAICS scope of regulated entities:** The final rule identifies the following NAICS codes as potentially regulated: 321113, 321211, 321212, 321215, 321219, and 321999. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Affected source definition:** The regulation defines "affected source" as "the collection of dryers, refiners, blenders, formers, presses, board coolers, and other process units associated with the manufacturing of plywood and composite wood products." The affected source "includes lumber kilns at PCWP manufacturing facilities and at any other kind of facility." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

---

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

**Definitional thresholds (FACT):** "Direct wood-fired PCWP dryer means a direct-fired PCWP dryer in which 10 percent or more of the direct-fired annual heat input results from combustion of wood-derived fuel" "in which greater than 90 percent of the direct-fired annual heat input results from natural gas (or propane) combustion." "a resin that contains less than 0.1 percent by mass of formaldehyde and less than 1.0 percent by mass each of phenol, methanol, and MDI." "purchased pre-dried to a moisture content of no more than 30 percent (weight percent, dry basis)" *Source: 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, eCFR. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

This section synthesizes the operative provisions of the July 6, 2026, final rule as enacted and codified in 40 CFR Part 63, Subpart DDDD, read in conjunction with the eCFR codified text and the 2020 RTR baseline.

### MACT Standards for Direct Wood-Fired PCWP Dryers

**FACT — Subcategorization basis:** The rule establishes two subcategories: (1) "direct wood-fired PCWP dryer" — "a direct-fired PCWP dryer in which 10 percent or more of the direct-fired annual heat input results from combustion of wood-derived fuel such as bark, wood residuals, or wood-derived syngas or any other fuel except for natural gas (or propane)" — and (2) "direct natural gas-fired PCWP dryer" — one "in which greater than 90 percent of the direct-fired annual heat input results from natural gas (or propane) combustion." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Emission limits for direct wood-fired dryers (Table 1D, existing sources, compliance by the applicable existing-source deadline):** The rule sets numeric PM (HAP metal), Hg, HCl, and PAH limits by dryer type. Selected limits include:
- Rotary strand dryer: PM 9.9E-02 lb/ODT or 3.6E-03 gr/dscf; Hg 1.7E-05 lb/ODT or 8.4E-04 mg/dscm; HCl 5.8E-03 lb/ODT or 1.5E-01 mg/dscm; PAH 1.1E-04 lb/ODT or 9.9E-03 mg/dscm.
- Green rotary dryer: PM 2.9E-01 lb/ODT or 5.2E-03 gr/dscf; Hg 1.5E-05 lb/ODT or 1.3E-03 mg/dscm; HCl 1.1E-02 lb/ODT or 1.7 mg/dscm; PAH 3.2E-04 lb/ODT or 4.2E-02 mg/dscm.
- Softwood veneer dryer heated zones: PM 7.2E-02 lb/MSF 3/8'' or 1.5E-02 gr/dscf; Hg 5.8E-05 lb/MSF 3/8'' or 4.1E-02 mg/dscm; HCl: not applicable (not detected); PAH: not applicable (burner tune-up standard applies).

*Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026, Table 3. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Naphthalene exclusion from PAH definition:** The final rule modifies the proposed PAH limits: "we removed naphthalene from the MACT floor analysis and from the rule specific definition of PAH at 40 CFR 63.2292." The enacted definition reads: "Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) means the sum of 2-methylnaphthalene, acenaphthylene, acenaphthene, fluorene, phenanthrene, anthracene, fluoranthene, pyrene, benz(a)anthracene, chrysene, benzo(b)fluoranthene, benzo(k)fluoranthene, benzo(e)pyrene, benzo(a)pyrene, perylene, indeno(1,2,3-c,d)pyrene, benzo(g,h,i)perylene, dibenz(a,h)anthracene." Naphthalene is explicitly excluded. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — D/F limit for green rotary dryers:** In addition to Table 1D limits, "direct wood-fired green rotary dryers that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before May 18, 2023, must limit emissions of dioxins and furans toxic equivalency (TEQ) to no more than 1.3E-09 pounds per oven dried ton (lb/ODT) or 1.7E-01 nanogram per dry standards cubic meter (ng/dscm) on and after July 6, 2029." For new sources (after May 18, 2023): "4.4E-10 lb/ODT or 3.7E-02 ng/dscm on and after July 6, 2029." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(3) and (4). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Work practice for softwood veneer dryer PAH:** "We are not finalizing the proposed PAH limits from softwood veneer dryers and instead are requiring PAH testing to be included in the performance tests of these dryers in addition to the burner tune-up standard." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Annual burner tune-up requirement for all direct-fired dryers:** The regulation requires "an annual tune-up of each combustion unit used to directly-fire the PCWP dryer or lumber kiln." "After the initial tune-up, each annual tune-up is required to be completed no more than 13 months after the previous tune-up." If the combustion unit is not operating on the required date, the tune-up is required "within 30 calendar days of startup." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(d). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Combustion unit bypass stack monitoring:** The rule requires continuous monitoring of "an indicator of bypass stack usage such as flow damper position or temperature" for combustion unit bypass stacks associated with direct-fired PCWP dryers and lumber kilns. Monitoring is required "at all times that the process unit or combustion unit (that routinely direct-fires a PCWP dryer or lumber kiln) is operating." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2269(k) and § 63.2270(g). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

### MACT Standards for Lumber Kilns

**FACT — Work practice basis for lumber kilns:** The EPA determined that "work practice standards for kilns are justified" because "the total volume of emissions cannot be emitted through a conveyance that is designed and constructed to emit or capture HAP emissions." The rule does not establish numeric emission limits for lumber kilns. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Four elements of the lumber kiln work practice (§ 63.2241(e)):**
1. O&M plan: "Develop and maintain onsite an O&M plan for the lumber kilns at the facility."
2. Annual burner tune-up for direct-fired kilns.
3. One of three work practice options: (i) temperature limit; (ii) hybrid (higher temperature + moisture monitoring); or (iii) site-specific plan.
4. Minimum kiln-dried lumber moisture content limits below which lumber is considered over-dried.

*Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(e). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Temperature limit option (Option i):** The regulation sets maximum dry bulb temperature limits of: "no more than 210 °F for batch indirect fired (IF) kilns, 235 °F for batch direct-fired (DF) kilns, 245 °F for continuous IF kilns, or 245 °F for continuous DF kilns." Compliance is demonstrated using "the batch cycle average dry bulb temperature (for batch kilns) or daily block average dry bulb temperature (for continuous kilns)." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(e)(3)(i). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Hybrid option temperature limits (Option ii):** Higher temperature ceilings of "no more than 240 °F for batch indirect fired (IF) kilns, 250 °F for batch direct-fired (DF) kilns, 260 °F for continuous IF kilns, or 260 °F for continuous DF kilns" apply — but only in combination with semiannual average lumber moisture content monitoring at or above the minimum limits in Table 11. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(e)(3)(ii). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Site-specific plan deadline:** "The site-specific plan must be developed and submitted to the delegated authority by the applicable site-specific-plan deadline." The plan must be "maintained onsite at the facility and is enforceable upon the compliance date." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2253(b). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — O&M plan inspection and corrective action timelines:** Inspection frequency is "no more than 13 months after the previous inspection." Corrective actions "must be initiated within 30 days after the inspection and completed within 180 days following the inspection identifying the need for the corrective action." Extension requests may be submitted to the delegated authority. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2253(a)(3). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Log vat temperature limit:** The rule requires that "each log vat" be operated "using a site-specific target log temperature that does not exceed 212 °F measured in the water used to soak the logs or in the wood as it is cut from the log." *Analytical inference:* a hot-water-surface-area coverage requirement proposed in an earlier rulemaking stage was NOT finalized. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(f). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

### MACT Standards for Process Units With Organic HAP Emissions

**FACT — Total HAP definition:** The regulation's own definition: "Total hazardous air pollutant emissions means, for purposes of this subpart, the sum of the emissions of the following six compounds: acetaldehyde, acrolein, formaldehyde, methanol, phenol, and propionaldehyde." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Atmospheric refiner emission limits (Table 1C):** Two subcategories are established:
- "Multipurpose atmospheric refiner" (all atmospheric refiners that are not post-dryer): existing sources 1.2E-01 lb/ODT or 15 ppmvd total HAP; new sources 2.4E-03 lb/ODT or 3.3 ppmvd.
- "Post-dryer atmospheric refiner" (defined by a majority-throughput-share test, source: eCFR; where the majority by weight of annual throughput has been previously dried onsite): existing sources 4.1E-03 lb/ODT or 8.5E-01 ppmvd; new sources 3.3E-03 lb/ODT or 6.5E-01 ppmvd.

*Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Table 1B option retained for certain process units:** "Affected facilities may choose to comply with the add-on control system compliance options in table 1B to this subpart (and associated operating limits in table 2 to this subpart) instead of the compliance options in table 1C to this subpart for fiberboard mat dryer heated zones, press predryers, post-dryer atmospheric refiners, or multipurpose atmospheric refiners." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(6). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — RMH process unit work practice — resin requirements:** Resinated material handling (RMH) process units — defined to include "resin tanks, softwood and hardwood plywood presses, engineered wood product presses and curing chambers, blenders, formers, finishing saws, finishing sanders, panel trim chippers, and reconstituted wood products board coolers (at existing affected sources), hardboard humidifiers, and onsite wastewater treatment operations specifically associated with PCWP manufacturing" — must meet one of three resin-related requirements: (i) use only a "non-HAP resin" (defined as "a resin that contains less than 0.1 percent by mass of formaldehyde and less than 1.0 percent by mass each of phenol, methanol, and MDI"); or (ii) use only a resin with maximum true vapor pressure ≤ 13.1 kPa (1.9 psia) for tanks with capacity less than 40,000 gallons, or < 5.2 kPa (0.75 psia) for tanks with capacity ≥ 40,000 gallons; or (iii) a combination of (i) and (ii). *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(g). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — RMH wood moisture requirement:** RMH process units must also "process wood material that was purchased pre-dried to a moisture content of no more than 30 percent (weight percent, dry basis), or has been dried in a dryer located at the PCWP facility." This requirement does not apply "for wet formers and onsite wastewater treatment operations specifically associated with PCWP manufacturing." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(g)(2). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Stand-alone digester work practice:** Facilities with stand-alone digesters must "use clean steam for injection into digestion process" and "process fiber without addition of HAP-containing or wood pulping chemicals." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 3, Row 11. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the relevant facility a "major source" under the definition in 40 CFR 63.2231(b)?**

FACT: The regulation defines major source as a facility emitting or having the potential to emit "any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2231(b). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific facility meets or exceeds these thresholds and therefore falls within the scope of Subpart DDDD.

**Q2: Is a given dryer a "direct wood-fired PCWP dryer" or a "direct natural gas-fired PCWP dryer"?**

FACT: The classification turns on the proportion of annual heat input from wood-derived fuel. "Direct wood-fired" applies when "10 percent or more of the direct-fired annual heat input results from combustion of wood-derived fuel." "Direct natural gas-fired" applies when "greater than 90 percent of the direct-fired annual heat input results from natural gas (or propane) combustion." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

*Legal Confirmation Required:* classification of dryers operating on mixed fuel regimes; this may be an unresolved definitional boundary for facilities with variable fuel blends.

**Q3: Is a given atmospheric refiner a "multipurpose atmospheric refiner" or a "post-dryer atmospheric refiner"?**

FACT: "Post-dryer atmospheric refiner means an atmospheric refiner used to process wood for use in PCWP in which 90 percent or more (by weight) of the annual throughput has been previously dried onsite in a dryer at the PCWP affected facility." All other atmospheric refiners are "multipurpose atmospheric refiners." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

*Legal Confirmation Required:* classification for facilities with mixed throughput where pre-dried feedstock is close to the applicable threshold.

**Q4: Is a given press subject to the MDI emission limits as an OSB press or a PB/MDF press?**

FACT: The subcategorization is by product type. The rule retains "the designated subcategorization based on the product type." OSB presses "are pressed at higher temperature" and "feed stocks (e.g., OSB are created with larger wood strands), which affect emission rates." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

*Legal Confirmation Required:* classification for presses that produce both product types on shared equipment.

**Q5: Does a facility qualify as a "new affected source" or "existing affected source"?**

FACT: The timing trigger is construction or reconstruction commencement relative to May 18, 2023. Sources whose construction commenced after May 18, 2023, face the July 6, 2026-or-startup compliance date; those commenced on or before May 18, 2023, face July 6, 2029. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2233(e). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

*Legal Confirmation Required:* classification of facilities that underwent partial reconstruction after May 18, 2023, where only specific process units were added or modified.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

### 1. Emission Limits — Direct Wood-Fired PCWP Dryers

**FACT — Existing source compliance date (Table 1D):** Dryers at sources with construction/reconstruction on or before May 18, 2023 — compliance required "on and after July 6, 2029." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(3). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — New source compliance date (Table 1E):** Dryers at sources with construction/reconstruction commenced after May 18, 2023 — compliance required "beginning on July 6, 2026, or upon initial startup, whichever is later." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(4). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Two-format compliance options:** Limits are set in both mass-per-production units (lb/ODT for most dryer types; lb/MSF 3/8'' for softwood veneer dryers) and concentration units (gr/dscf for PM; mg/dscm for non-PM pollutants). Facilities may comply using either format. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — D/F limits only for green rotary dryers:** Among direct wood-fired dryer types, only green rotary dryers are subject to numeric D/F TEQ limits. All other direct wood-fired dryer types are subject to burner tune-up work practices for D/F control — not numeric D/F limits. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026, footnote (e) to Table 3. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

### 2. Emission Limits — Process Units with Organic HAP (Table 1C)

**FACT — Fiberboard mat dryers (existing sources only):** Applicable to "an affected source that commenced construction or reconstruction on or before January 9, 2003." Limit: 4.9E-02 lb total HAP/MSF 1/8'' or 2.0E-01 lb total HAP/MSF 1/2''. New sources are already subject to Table 1A or 1B limits. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 1C, footnote 2. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Press predryers (existing sources only):** Same construction date condition as fiberboard mat dryers (on or before January 9, 2003). Limit: 8.0E-02 lb total HAP/MSF 1/8'' or 3.2E-01 lb total HAP/MSF 1/2''. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 1C. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Mixed PCWP process streams:** Streams that were commingled with Table 1B-regulated streams before July 6, 2026, "must continue to comply with the compliance options in table 1B to this subpart after July 6, 2026." These are defined as "an emission stream from a process unit subject to standards effective on July 6, 2026, that was co-mingled with an emissions stream or streams from one or more process units subject to the compliance options in table 1B to this subpart before July 6, 2026, at an affected source that commenced construction (or reconstruction) on or before May 18, 2023." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(5) and § 63.2292. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

### 3. Performance Testing Requirements

**FACT — Initial performance test deadline:** "The final rule requires initial performance tests to be completed within 180 days after the compliance date for the new standards." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Repeat performance testing frequency:** "Subsequent performance testing every five years (60 months), thereafter." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Test methods (Table 4):** Key methods include EPA Method 320 or NCASI methods for total HAP; EPA Method 326 for MDI (minimum sample volume 1 dscm); EPA Method 5 or 29 for PM (minimum 2 dscm); EPA Method 29 or 30B for Hg; EPA Method 26A for HCl (minimum 2 dscm); EPA Method 23 for PAH and D/F (minimum 3 dscm); ASTM D6348-12e1 as an acceptable alternative to EPA Method 320 with specified caveats. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 4. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Scope and timing:** After July 6, 2026 (new sources) or July 6, 2029 (existing sources), facilities must "continuously monitor usage of the process unit bypass stack at all times while the process units are operating." These obligations fall on facility owners/operators, not on freight forwarders. They are documented here as context for commercial relationships with PCWP facilities.

"Notifications of Compliance Status must be submitted in a user-specified format such as portable document format (PDF) following the procedure specified in § 63.9(k)." *Operational implication:* this NOCS filing obligation runs to the facility owner/operator, not to a freight forwarder counterpart. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2280(d). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Bypass stack usage reporting:** The semiannual compliance report must include "the total time (hours) during the semiannual reporting period that each combustion unit bypass stack or each process unit bypass stack was used." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2281(c)(10). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Burner tune-up reporting:** The semiannual compliance report must include "the date of the most recent burner tune-up and a summary of corrective actions taken." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2281(c)(9). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

# 11. Operational System Requirements

These requirements apply to PCWP facility operators. They are documented here to inform commercial and operational planning with PCWP facility counterparts.

### Continuous Monitoring Systems

**FACT — WESP monitoring:** For wet electrostatic precipitators, the 3-hour block average total secondary electric power input and liquid flow rate must be maintained above minimum limits established during performance testing. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 2, Row 6. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Dry ESP monitoring:** 3-hour block average total secondary electric power input above minimum limit, or alternatively, 24-hour block average opacity ≤ 10 percent (or highest hourly average during performance test). *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 2, Row 7. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Electrified filter bed (EFB) monitoring:** "Maintain the 3-hour block average ionizer voltage and the bed voltage above the minimum limits established during the performance test; AND maintain the pressure drop within the range established during the performance test." The final rule corrected a typographical error: "only voltage monitoring is required for EFB." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 2, Row 10; Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Mechanical collector or other dry control device (not listed elsewhere in Table 2):** Two options: (a) maintain 24-hour block average opacity ≤ 10 percent (or highest hourly average during test) using a COMS; or (b) maintain 3-hour block average pressure drop above minimum AND weekly 6-minute opacity observations below the maximum established in § 63.2262(u). *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, Table 2, Row 11. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Lumber kiln temperature monitoring location:** "For purposes of complying with dry bulb temperature limits in § 63.2241(e)(3)(i) or (ii), dry bulb temperature monitor(s) must be located in a position to determine the dry bulb temperature of the heated air that exits the lumber." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2269(m)(1). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Lumber moisture monitoring frequency (hybrid option):** For lumber moisture measured after the kiln: "at least one lumber moisture content measurement per either twenty thousand board feet (20 MBF or 20,000 BF) of board lumber produced or per 2,000 cubic feet (2,000 CF) of round lumber produced." For batch kilns with in-kiln monitoring: "at least one lumber moisture reading per crib." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2269(n). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Flow sensor calibration frequency:** The final rule changed from semiannual to annual: "Conduct a flow sensor calibration check at least annually." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2269(h)(4). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

*Operational implication:* PCWP facilities now face significant new monitoring infrastructure requirements — continuous bypass stack monitors, lumber kiln temperature monitoring systems, moisture meters at specified locations, and APCD parameter monitoring — all of which must be commissioned and verified within 180 days of the applicable compliance date. Facilities that have not yet assessed their monitoring gaps face a compressed implementation window before the July 6, 2029, deadline for existing sources.

---

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*Analytical inference:* **FACT — Combustion units accepting process exhausts into the flame zone — exemption from performance testing:** "Combustion units that accept process exhausts into the flame zone are exempt from the performance testing to show compliance with the compliance options in table 1B or 1C to this subpart and the operating requirements for thermal oxidizers." Documentation showing that "process exhausts controlled by the combustion unit enter into the flame zone" must be submitted with the NOCS. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2260(a) and § 63.2262(k)(3). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Wet scrubber, EFB, and mechanical collector pressure drop during startup/shutdown:** "When using a wet scrubber, electrified filter bed, or mechanical collector (or other dry control device not mentioned elsewhere in table 2 to this subpart), you are not required to meet the minimum limit for pressure drop across the control device during startup or shutdown. Parameter limits other than pressure drop continue to apply during startup and shutdown." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2250(f)(7). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Work practices for safety-related shutdowns, pressurized refiner startup/shutdown, and direct-fired softwood veneer dryer gas-fired burner startup/shutdown:** These three specific operating conditions each have separate work practice standards (Table 3, Rows 6, 7, 8) that apply in lieu of the otherwise applicable compliance options. "The otherwise applicable compliance options, operating requirements, and work practice requirements (in rows 1 through 5 of table 3 to this subpart) do not apply during the operating conditions specified in paragraphs (f)(2) through (4) of this section, with the exception of the operating requirement in § 63.2240(e) which applies at all times." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2250(f)(6). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Stand-alone digester and fiber washer — no numeric limits (work practice only):** The EPA determined that stand-alone digesters and fiber washers "meet the criteria under CAA section 112(h)(2)(B) for establishing a work practice standard because there are technological and economic limitations to measuring emissions." No PCWP affected sources are currently expected to operate these units, given the closure of the only then-operating wet/dry hardboard facility, but standards are finalized for future applicability. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Biofilter installation — 180-day grace period:** "For a new biofilter installation, you will be allowed up to 180 days following the compliance date or 180 days following initial startup of the biofilter to complete the requirements in paragraph (m)(1) of this section." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2262(m)(2). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — RMH wood moisture requirement exemption for wet formers and wastewater operations:** "This paragraph (g)(2) does not apply for wet formers and onsite wastewater treatment operations specifically associated with PCWP manufacturing." *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2241(g)(2). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

**FACT — Table 1B option in lieu of Table 1C:** Existing affected facilities may choose Table 1B add-on control system compliance (with associated Table 2 operating limits) as an alternative to Table 1C for fiberboard mat dryer heated zones, press predryers, post-dryer atmospheric refiners, or multipurpose atmospheric refiners. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2240(d)(6). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD

---

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

**FACT — Emissions reduction and co-benefit estimates:** The final rule is estimated to "reduce 721 tpy of directly-regulated HAPs compared to baseline emissions of 7,250 tpy." Additional co-benefit reductions are estimated at "approximately 8,504 tpy" of VOC, "202 tpy of PM, 144 tpy of PM 2.5, 132 tpy of NOx, 719 tpy of CO, 12 tpy of SO2." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — 2020 RTR health risk baseline:** The 2020 RTR established that "the maximum individual cancer risk was 30-in-1 million for actual and allowable emissions and the noncancer hazard indices for chronic exposure were below 1 (i.e., 0.8 for actual and allowable emissions). The maximum noncancer hazard quotient for acute exposure was 4." The 2026 rule builds on this baseline by reducing the emission profile further. *Source: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — Non-HAP resin alternatives:** The rule's RMH work practice framework is built around the availability of non-HAP resins. "Non-HAP resin means a resin that contains less than 0.1 percent by mass of formaldehyde and less than 1.0 percent by mass each of phenol, methanol, and MDI." The EPA noted in the 2020 RTR that some PCWP facilities had already shifted toward lower-HAP resin systems to comply with CARB and TSCA formaldehyde product standards, though these were not characterized as a "development" compelling standard revision. *Source: eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, § 63.2292; Federal Register Vol. 85, No. 157, August 13, 2020. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2020/08/13/2020-12725/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

**FACT — WESP/RTO as prevalent control configuration:** "Most of the direct wood-fired rotary strand dryer systems at major sources in the U.S. already operate with PM and HAP control technology (e.g., wet electrostatic precipitator followed by a regenerative thermal oxidizer, WESP/RTO)." The use of WESPs is described as prevalent "because of the high moisture exhaust stream and nature of the particulate originating from dryers (e.g., sticky, flammable)." *Source: Federal Register Vol. 88, No. 96, May 18, 2023. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/18/2023-10067/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

---

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

| Date | Milestone |
|---|---|
| July 30, 2004 | Original PCWP NESHAP promulgated (69 FR 45944). |
| 2007 | D.C. Circuit vacated and remanded "no-control" MACT floor determinations (NRDC v. EPA, 489 F.3d 1364). |
| August 13, 2020 | 2020 RTR final rule effective; SSM exemptions removed; electronic reporting and repeat testing added (85 FR 49434). |
| August 13, 2021 | Existing-source compliance date for 2020 RTR amendments, including safety-related shutdown and pressurized refiner work practices. |
| May 18, 2023 | Proposed rule published (88 FR 31856); public comment period opened. |
| July 18, 2023 | Public comment period closed. |
| **July 6, 2026** | **Final rule effective. New/reconstructed sources (construction commenced after May 18, 2023) must comply with all new standards immediately or upon startup, whichever is later.** |
| **~August 5, 2026** | **NOCS due for mixed PCWP process streams (no later than 30 days after July 6, 2026 publication).** |
| **September 4, 2026** | **Deadline to file D.C. Circuit petition for judicial review of the July 6, 2026, final rule.** |
| **January 6, 2028** | **Deadline for lumber kilns choosing the site-specific plan option to develop and submit the plan to the delegated authority.** |
| **July 6, 2029** | **Existing affected sources (construction/reconstruction on or before May 18, 2023) must comply with all new emission limits and work practices.** |
| **December 5, 2029** (180 days after July 6, 2029) | **Initial performance tests due for existing sources under new standards.** |
| ~2034 | *Analytical inference:* Next CAA section 112(d)(6) technology review window opens (8-year cycle from 2026 final rule). |

*Source for all dated milestones: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 127, July 6, 2026; eCFR, 40 CFR Part 63 Subpart DDDD, §§ 63.2233(e), 63.2253(b)(1); Federal Register Vol. 85, No. 157, August 13, 2020. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13550/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-63/subpart-DDDD; https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2020/08/13/2020-12725/national-emission-standards-for-hazardous-air-pollutants-plywood-and-composite-wood-products

---

# 15. Sources
