entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document provides a regulatory fact brief on the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) Order 2024 (the "SAF Order"), a UK statutory instrument implementing Chapter 5 of Part 2 of the Energy Act 2004. The brief is anchored to the operational context of a global freight forwarding workspace whose primary transport mode is air. All binding-obligation language is either verbatim from the source text and cited inline, or labeled as analytical inference, operational implication, or legal confirmation required. No claim is made as to whether this specific workspace holds any defined legal role under the Order; that determination is routed to *Legal Confirmation Required:* callouts throughout.

**Conventions used:** FACT statements are drawn verbatim or near-verbatim from the enacted text. ANALYSIS statements are prefixed with one of three closed-set label tokens. Legal conclusions are routed to *Legal Confirmation Required:* callouts. Required slots (effective date, primary deadline, jurisdictional scope, penalty summary) are each explicitly addressed.

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**What it is:**

The SAF Order is a UK statutory instrument made under the Energy Act 2004. It imposes what the Order terms a "SAF obligation" — a renewable transport fuel obligation — on aviation fuel suppliers. The Order's explanatory note states: "This Order implements Chapter 5 of Part 2 of the Energy Act 2004, and imposes an obligation on aviation fuel suppliers that supply aviation turbine fuel in the United Kingdom to produce evidence that a specified amount of sustainable aviation fuel has been supplied in the United Kingdom."

*Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) Order 2024, Explanatory Note, UK Draft Statutory Instruments 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Effective date (required slot):**

Article 1(1) states: "This Order may be cited as the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) Order 2024 and comes into force on 1st January 2025." *Source: Article 1(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Jurisdictional scope (required slot):**

Article 1(2) states: "This Order extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland." *Source: Article 1(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Why it is relevant to air freight operations:**

The Order defines "supplier" as "a person that, in the course of their business, supplies aviation fuel at or for delivery to places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 2(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating in air freight supply chains that interact with aviation fuel supply at UK airports — whether as operators of aircraft, or as parties whose operations cause aviation turbine fuel to be placed into commercial aviation supply chains — should assess whether any entity in their chain meets the Order's definition of "supplier." The obligation falls on defined "suppliers," not on freight forwarders generically; the chain-position question is a legal one.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, or any carrier it uses, meets the defined term "supplier" — "a person that, in the course of their business, supplies aviation fuel at or for delivery to places in the United Kingdom" — and thereby holds SAF obligations under the Order, requires legal review against the workspace's specific contractual and operational arrangements at UK airports.

**Primary deadline (required slot):**

The first obligation period runs for one calendar year from the Order's effective date. The specified date by which SAF certificates (evidence) must be produced or a buy-out payment made is defined as "15th September of the year immediately following an obligation period (or the next working day after 15th September if 15th September is not a working day)." *Analytical inference:* applying the rule to the first obligation period yields a reporting deadline in the September following that period's end. *Source: Article 3(3), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

---

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**1. Assess whether any air carrier or aviation fuel supplier used by the workspace is an "obligated supplier" under the Order — and how this flows through to freight costs.** MONITORING → COST ALERT

The Order imposes a buy-out payment obligation on obligated suppliers who cannot discharge their SAF obligation by producing SAF certificates. The buy-out rate is: PtL obligation shortfall multiplied by £0.145 per MJ, plus main obligation shortfall multiplied by £0.137 per MJ. *Source: Article 21(9), Steps 3 and 4, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* Carriers and aviation fuel suppliers facing a SAF shortfall will incur buy-out costs beginning with the first obligation year, due in the September following that year. These costs will be a mechanism for cost pass-through to air freight clients. Workspaces moving time-sensitive or high-value cargo on UK air routes should assess carrier conversations around SAF surcharges.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any buy-out cost constitutes a lawful surcharge passable to shippers requires carrier-specific legal and commercial review.

**Action:** Engage key UK air carrier partners now to understand their SAF obligation status and whether SAF cost surcharges are planned for 2025–2026 freight pricing. Request written disclosure.

---

**2. Verify whether the workspace's Scope 3 emissions reporting reflects SAF blending volumes on UK routes.** ACTION REQUIRED

The Order establishes a trajectory of SAF blending obligations that will alter the carbon intensity of aviation turbine fuel supplied in the UK. The main obligation percentages (applied to the "obligated amount") are: 2.041% in 2025, rising to 23.718% by 2040 and subsequent periods. *Source: Article 3(7), Table, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* Workspaces reporting Scope 3 aviation emissions under client sustainability frameworks will need to determine how SAF-blended aviation turbine fuel on UK routes affects their emissions factors. The carbon intensity formula embedded in the Order (Article 4(4)) uses a fossil jet fuel reference of 89gCO2e/MJ and a SAF reference carbon intensity of 26.7 gCO2e/MJ. *Source: Article 4(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Action:** Map current Scope 3 air emissions methodology against SAF blend volumes on UK routes. Assess whether carrier data will be available to distinguish SAF-blended fuel in emissions accounting from 2025 onward.

---

**3. Monitor the administrator's publication of guidance under Article 14(1)(f) — this guidance is the operational key to SAF sustainability criteria, GHG calculations, and lower heating values.** MONITORING

The Order's Administrator (the Secretary of State for Transport) is required to publish guidance covering: additional sustainability information; GHG emissions savings methodology; default and actual values; lower heating values of aviation fuels; soil carbon, land, forest, and sustainable waste management criteria; and carbon capture requirements for hydrogen from fossil wastes. *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(i)–(ix), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* Until this guidance is published, obligated suppliers and their supply chains cannot fully operationalize sustainability criteria or GHG calculations. The guidance is a prerequisite to issuing SAF certificates, which are the primary compliance mechanism.

**Action:** Set a 60-day re-check to verify whether the Administrator has published guidance under Article 14(1)(f). If not published by an early month of the first obligation period, escalate to carrier partners who are obligated suppliers for status.

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The SAF Order places obligations on "suppliers" — defined as "a person that, in the course of their business, supplies aviation fuel at or for delivery to places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 2(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The Order distinguishes between "obligated suppliers" (those on whom a SAF obligation is imposed under Article 3) and "non-obligated suppliers" (all other suppliers). *Source: Article 2(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

A SAF obligation arises only for suppliers meeting the volume threshold: Article 3(1) and (2) state that a SAF obligation is imposed on every supplier that, in a specified period, "supplies relevant aviation turbine fuel," but "does not apply to a supplier that, in a specified period, supplies an amount of relevant aviation turbine fuel that has a total energy content of less than 15.9 terajoules." *Source: Article 3(1)–(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The Order defines "relevant aviation turbine fuel" as "aviation turbine fuel owned by a supplier at the assessment time and supplied by that supplier at, or for delivery to, places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 2(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, or its airline and fuel supply chain partners, falls within the defined term "supplier" — and whether the workspace itself is exposed to direct SAF obligations as opposed to downstream cost pass-through — requires legal review against specific operational arrangements. Freight forwarders do not typically "supply aviation fuel" in the ordinary sense, but the workspace should confirm this with counsel given the breadth of the definition.

*Operational implication:* In the most common freight forwarding arrangement, the direct compliance burden falls on the aviation fuel supplier (e.g., fuel company) and potentially on the aircraft operator if it meets the "supplier" definition in the context of UK fuel supply. The workspace's primary exposure is indirect: cost pass-through from obligated suppliers, and the accuracy of its own emissions reporting where SAF blending alters the carbon intensity of UK aviation fuel.

---

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Order requires the Administrator to publish specific guidance under Article 14(1)(f). As of the date of this brief, no separate published guidance document was available in the source corpus provided.

*Specific guidance published by the Administrator under Article 14(1)(f) not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.* The Order is explicit that sustainability criteria operationalization, GHG methodology, lower heating values, and land/forest/soil carbon/sustainable waste management criteria all depend on this guidance. *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(i)–(ix), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* Until the Administrator publishes this guidance, the full operational implementation of the SAF obligation by UK suppliers remains incomplete. Workspaces should treat this guidance publication as a key monitoring trigger.

Key anticipated guidance content (as defined by the Order itself):

- **Additional sustainability information:** The specific information required beyond the sustainability criteria; defined in guidance under Article 14(1)(f)(i). *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(i), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- **GHG emissions savings methodology:** Including how default values and actual values are determined for renewable transport fuel and recycled carbon fuel; required under Article 14(1)(f)(iii) and (ix). *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(iii) and (ix), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- **Lower heating values:** The energy content figures (MJ/kg) for aviation fuels, which are embedded in all obligated-amount and SAF-amount calculations. *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(viii), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- **Land, forest, soil carbon, and sustainable waste criteria:** How the Administrator will assess compliance with Schedule 1 (sustainability criteria), Schedule 2 (land criteria), and Schedule 3 (forest criteria). *Source: Article 14(1)(f)(ii), (iv), (v), (vi), (vii), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

---

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1. Administrator guidance under Article 14(1)(f) — publication date not specified in the Order.** MONITORING

The Order mandates that the Administrator (Secretary of State for Transport) publish guidance on the matters listed in Article 14(1)(f), but does not specify a publication deadline. *Source: Article 14(1)(f), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* Given that the Order came into force on the Order's effective date and the first obligation period ends the end of the first obligation period, guidance must be published sufficiently in advance of the SAF certificate application deadline to be actionable. Re-check window: an early month of the first obligation period.

**2. Designation of wastes of fossil origin as relevant feedstocks — Administrator determination required.** MONITORING

Article 15(1) states the Administrator "must determine the wastes of fossil origin that may be used in the production of a recycled carbon fuel and designate each such waste as a relevant feedstock," and must publish a list. *Source: Article 15(1) and (3), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714 No publication date is specified.

**3. Replacement draft — this draft has been superseded.** ACTION REQUIRED

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the entity in the workspace's air supply chain a "supplier" under the Order?**

The Order defines "supplier" as "a person that, in the course of their business, supplies aviation fuel at or for delivery to places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 2(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a specific airline, fuel company, or handling agent in the workspace's UK operations meets this definition — and therefore holds a SAF obligation — is a legal determination requiring counsel review against their specific commercial arrangements.

---

**Q2: Does the 15.9 TJ threshold exempt smaller fuel suppliers?**

The Order states a SAF obligation "does not apply to a supplier that, in a specified period, supplies an amount of relevant aviation turbine fuel that has a total energy content of less than 15.9 terajoules." *Source: Article 3(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces using smaller regional airports or niche charter operators, the carriers or fuel suppliers serving those routes may fall below the 15.9 TJ threshold, meaning no SAF obligation would apply and no cost pass-through mechanism would exist under this Order for those routes.

---

**Q3: Does the obligation apply to aviation gasoline (Avgas) as well as aviation turbine fuel (ATF/Jet fuel)?**

The Order's SAF obligation in Article 3(1) applies to suppliers of "relevant aviation turbine fuel" — specifically "aviation turbine fuel owned by a supplier at the assessment time and supplied by that supplier at, or for delivery to, places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 2(1) definition of "relevant aviation turbine fuel," SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The obligation is calculated against "relevant aviation turbine fuel" only. Aviation gasoline (Avgas) is a separately defined term but does not appear in the obligation calculation provisions. *Source: Article 3(4)–(8), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* The core volume-based obligation is anchored to aviation turbine fuel (jet fuel), not aviation gasoline. Operations using piston-engine aircraft (Avgas) are not within the SAF obligation's volume calculation trigger.

---

**Q4: Does hydrogen used in hydroprocessing count toward the relevant feedstock percentage?**

The Order explicitly addresses this: Article 4(5)(b) states "where hydrogen is used for hydroprocessing during the production of aviation fuel, RF is to be determined by excluding that hydrogen," while Article 4(5)(c) states "where hydrogen is physically incorporated into synthetic aviation fuel during its production, RF is to be determined by including that hydrogen." *Source: Article 4(5)(b)–(c), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

---

**Q5: Does the Order apply to sustainable aviation fuel that has already been counted under another support scheme?**

No. A condition for SAF certificate issuance is that "the applicable sustainable aviation fuel, or a chemical precursor to it, has not already been, and will not be, counted under a support scheme, or a United Kingdom renewable energy obligation other than the SAF obligation of the supplier." *Source: Article 16(3)(f), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Penalty summary slot (FACT):** "A supplier is liable for a civil penalty if that supplier contravenes article 6(2) or 21(8)." *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) Order 2024. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2024/995/contents/made

Step 4 Multiply the main obligation shortfall by £0.137" The carry-forward limit states: "may count towards the discharge of no more than 25% of a supplier’s main obligation" *Source: The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligations (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) Order 2024. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2024/995/contents/made

### A. The SAF Obligation — Structure and Calculation

The SAF obligation has two components per obligation period:

**Main obligation:** "A supplier's main obligation for an obligation period … is the amount of sustainable aviation fuel that has a total energy content equal to the percentage of the supplier's obligated amount for that period" as set out in column 2 of the Article 3(7) table. *Source: Article 3(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**Power-to-liquid (PtL) obligation:** "A supplier's power-to-liquid aviation fuel obligation for an obligation period … is the amount of power-to-liquid aviation fuel that has a total energy content equal to the percentage of the supplier's obligated amount for that period" as set out in column 3 of the Article 3(7) table. *Source: Article 3(5), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

**The full obligation trajectory (Article 3(7) table):**

| Obligation Period | Main Obligation % | PtL Obligation % |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 2.041% | 0.000% |
| 2026 | 3.734% | 0.000% |
| 2027 | 5.485% | 0.000% |
| 2028 | 7.082% | 0.215% |
| 2029 | 8.952% | 0.218% |
| 2030 | 10.556% | 0.556% |
| 2031 | 11.485% | 0.560% |
| 2032 | 12.465% | 0.850% |
| 2033 | 13.467% | 1.146% |
| 2034 | 14.493% | 1.449% |
| 2035 | 15.882% | 1.765% |
| 2036 | 17.344% | 2.273% |
| 2037 | 18.856% | 2.798% |
| 2038 | 20.421% | 3.342% |
| 2039 | 22.040% | 3.904% |
| 2040 and subsequent | 23.718% | 4.487% |

*Source: Article 3(7), Table, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* The PtL sub-obligation begins only from 2028, with no power-to-liquid aviation fuel obligation in 2025–2027. Power-to-liquid aviation fuel is the highest-cost SAF pathway; the cost pass-through trajectory for UK air freight accelerates materially from 2028 onward.

### B. The Obligated Amount — Calculation Basis and Threshold Deduction

The "obligated amount" is calculated by the following steps:
- Calculate the notional amount of relevant aviation turbine fuel supplied during the obligation period (formula at Article 3(8)).
- "if the notional amount has a total energy content of less than 344 terajoules, deduct the first 15.9 terajoules of that amount." *Source: Article 3(6), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* The 15.9 TJ deduction is a small-supplier threshold credit embedded in the calculation basis, not merely an exemption trigger. Suppliers above the 344 TJ threshold do not receive the deduction.

The notional amount formula (Article 3(8)) accounts for the lower heating value of aviation turbine fuel and adjusts for the mass of SAF supplied versus conventional fuel, applying the relevant feedstock fraction and sustainability criteria compliance fractions. *Source: Article 3(8), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### C. SAF Amount Calculation — The Carbon Intensity Multiplier

For the purpose of discharging a SAF obligation or issuing SAF certificates, the notional amount of relevant sustainable aviation fuel (Article 4(4)) incorporates a carbon intensity multiplier using:

- **CF** = 89gCO2e/MJ (average lifecycle carbon intensity of fossil jet fuel)
- **CS** = lifecycle carbon intensity (in gCO2e/MJ) of the relevant sustainable aviation fuel supplied (the SAF reference value stated elsewhere in this Order is 26.7 gCO2e/MJ)
- **CR** = the SAF reference value stated above (average reference lifecycle carbon intensity of sustainable aviation fuel)

*Source: Article 4(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* The carbon intensity multiplier means that lower-carbon-intensity SAF generates proportionally more certificate credit per kilogram supplied. This creates an incentive structure favoring the lowest-carbon SAF pathways, and will affect how carrier SAF procurement strategies are structured.

### D. Sustainability Criteria (Schedule 1)

Relevant sustainable aviation fuel only counts toward discharging a SAF obligation if it "meets the sustainability criteria." *Source: Article 4(3), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The sustainability criteria in Schedule 1 set out a GHG emissions saving threshold for each feedstock category. The minimum GHG emissions saving "is the greater of — (a) where applicable, the default value determined by reference to the guidance published by the Administrator under article 14(1)(f); or (b) the actual value determined by reference to the guidance published by the Administrator under article 14(1)(f)." *Source: Schedule 1, paragraph 7, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The feedstock-specific sustainability conditions (summarised from Schedule 1, paragraph 2 table):

- Forest biomass: GHG emissions saving threshold AND forest criteria.
- Processing residues (non-agriculture/aquaculture/fisheries/forestry): GHG emissions saving threshold only.
- Wastes of biological origin (non-agriculture etc.): GHG emissions saving threshold only.
- Residues/wastes from agriculture: GHG emissions saving threshold, land criteria, AND soil carbon criteria.
- Renewable non-biomass or nuclear energy: GHG emissions saving threshold only.
- Wastes of fossil origin: GHG emissions saving threshold, land criteria, AND sustainable waste criteria.
- All other feedstocks: GHG emissions saving threshold AND land criteria.

*Source: Schedule 1, paragraph 2, Table, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### E. Segregated Oils and Fats Cap (Article 22)

The maximum amount of relevant sustainable aviation fuel derived from segregated oils and fats that may count toward an obligated supplier's main obligation is capped. The cap trajectory:

| Obligation Period | Cap (% of relevant ATF supplied) |
|---|---|
| 2025 | 2.00% |
| 2026 | 3.60% |
| 2027 | 4.80% |
| 2028 | 5.80% |
| 2029 | 6.60% |
| 2030 | 7.10% |
| 2031 | 7.50% |
| 2032 | 7.60% |
| 2033 | 7.70% |
| 2034 | 7.70% |
| 2035 and subsequent | 7.80% |

*Source: Article 22, Table, SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* The segregated oils and fats cap reflects policy concern about supply constraints and land-use competition from feedstocks like used cooking oil. The cap is set at a level that tracks — but slightly undercuts — the main obligation percentage, particularly in the early years.

### F. Certificate Banking — Use in Later Obligation Periods (Article 23)

SAF certificates issued for one obligation period may be carried forward, subject to strict limits:

- "Any SAF certificate may count towards the discharge of no more than 25% of a supplier's main obligation in the next obligation period." *Source: Article 23(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- "A SAF certificate for power-to-liquid aviation fuel may count towards the discharge of no more than 25% of a supplier's power-to-liquid aviation fuel obligation in the next obligation period." *Source: Article 23(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- "A SAF certificate for sustainable aviation fuel derived from segregated oils and fats may count towards the discharge of no more than 25% of the maximum amount of sustainable aviation fuel derived from segregated oils and fats that may count towards the discharge of the supplier's main obligation … in the next obligation period." *Source: Article 23(3), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

Certificates may only be carried into the "next obligation period" — defined as "the obligation period immediately following the obligation period for which the SAF certificate was issued." *Source: Article 23(5), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### G. Definition of "Sustainable Aviation Fuel" — the types in scope

The Order defines "sustainable aviation fuel" as "aviation fuel which is a liquid or gaseous renewable transport fuel" of the following specified types:
- "(a) aviation gasoline;
- (b) aviation turbine fuel; and
- (c) subject to paragraph (2), hydrogen."

For hydrogen produced using wastes of fossil origin, it is only treated as a specified type "if the carbon emitted during its production is captured and stored in a manner determined by the Administrator and published in guidance under article 14(1)(f)." *Source: Article 2(1) and 2(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### H. Recycled Carbon Fuel and Nuclear-Derived Fuel designations

"For the purposes of section 131D(1)(a) of the 2004 Act, sustainable aviation fuel produced wholly from wastes of fossil origin designated as a relevant feedstock is designated as a recycled carbon fuel." *Source: Article 2(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

"For the purposes of section 131D(1)(b) of the 2004 Act, energy-derived aviation fuel produced wholly from nuclear sources is designated as a nuclear-derived fuel." *Source: Article 2(5), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* the obligation trajectory, buy-out mechanics and carbon-intensity reference values above run to fuel suppliers as the regulated entity; a workspace should track its fuel supplier's SAF compliance posture rather than expect a direct obligation on itself.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Operational implication:* the registration and reporting obligations below run to fuel suppliers, not to freight forwarders directly.

### SAF Account Registration

Article 6(2) states a person "must apply for an account under paragraph (1)(b) not later than the end of the period of 28 days beginning on the date on which the person becomes an obligated supplier." *Source: Article 6(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

Non-obligated suppliers and other persons intending to trade or invest in SAF certificates may apply for an account at the Administrator's discretion, subject to demonstrating "good reason to hold an account" and consenting to Administrator access to premises, computers, records, or documents. *Source: Article 6(3)–(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### Information Reporting by Suppliers

The Administrator requires each obligated supplier (and any non-obligated supplier applying for a SAF certificate) to provide, by the specified date (15 September of the year following the obligation period), information including:

- Whether relevant aviation turbine fuel and relevant sustainable aviation fuel were supplied during each relevant period.
- The amounts (mass in kilograms, energy content) of each fuel type supplied or received.
- For partially sustainable aviation fuel: mass attributable to relevant feedstocks.
- Compliance of sustainable aviation fuel with sustainability criteria, excluding non-relevant-feedstock mass.
- Mass meeting sustainability criteria.
- Additional sustainability information.
- For power-to-liquid aviation fuel: evidence that the fuel meets the PtL definition.

*Source: Article 11(1)(a)–(c), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### Verification Requirements

For SAF certificate applications:

- A **verifier's assurance report** (meeting Article 17(1) requirements — limited assurance under ISAE 3000 or equivalent, by a qualified third party who is not the supplier or a connected person) is required for information relating to sustainability criteria compliance. *Source: Article 16(3)(c) and Article 17(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714
- A **verifier's declaration** (reasonable assurance under ISAE 3000 or equivalent) is required confirming the accuracy of information related to the amount of sustainable aviation fuel. *Source: Article 16(3)(d) and Article 17(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The Administrator may upgrade the verifier's assurance report requirement from limited to reasonable assurance if it chooses. *Source: Article 17(4), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### SAF Certificate Application Deadline

Applications for SAF certificates must be made "by 12th May of the year immediately following the obligation period (or the next working day after 12th May, if 12th May is not a working day); or such later date as the Administrator may notify." *Analytical inference:* the application deadline for the first obligation period falls in the spring following that period, per the Administrator's published schedule. *Source: Article 16(3)(h), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

# 11. Operational System Requirements

### Mass Balance System (mandatory for obligated suppliers)

Article 13(1) states "A supplier must use a mass balance system in accordance with this article for the purposes of producing any information which the supplier is required to provide, or evidence which the supplier is required to produce, under articles 11(6) and 12(5)." *Source: Article 13(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

The Order defines "mass balance system" as one which: "(a) allows amounts of relevant feedstock or fuel with different sustainability characteristics to be mixed ('the mixture'); (b) provides for the sustainability characteristics of amounts added to the mixture to be attributed to other amounts withdrawn from the mixture; and (c) requires the sustainability characteristics attributed to the sum of the amounts withdrawn from the mixture to be the same, and in the same quantities, as the sustainability characteristics attributed to the sum of the amounts added to the mixture." *Source: Article 13(5), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Operational implication:* For workspaces whose carrier partners are obligated suppliers, the mass balance requirement means fuel sustainability data must be tracked and matched across the entire fuel supply chain. This has implications for the quality and granularity of sustainability data that carriers will need to provide to support Scope 3 reporting.

### Electronic Account and Certificate Management

Article 6(8) states accounts "must be established and maintained in electronic form or in such other form as the Administrator determines is appropriate (or in both forms)." *Source: Article 6(8), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

Article 16(1) requires SAF certificate applications "in electronic form, through a website of the Administrator," unless the Administrator permits another form. *Source: Article 16(1), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces operating their own Scope 3 or sustainability reporting systems, the digital-first infrastructure of the SAF certificate registry is a signal that structured data extraction from carrier partners (e.g., SAF certificate numbers, fuel mass, LHV values, carbon intensities) will eventually need to be built into reporting workflows.

### Administrator's Website for Certificate Transfers

Article 19(2)(b) requires certificate transfer notifications "through a website of the Administrator, or in another manner, in a case where the Administrator determines that it is appropriate." *Source: Article 19(2)(b), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

### Small Supplier Exemption

Article 3(2): The SAF obligation "does not apply to a supplier that, in a specified period, supplies an amount of relevant aviation turbine fuel that has a total energy content of less than 15.9 terajoules." *Source: Article 3(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* This threshold exempts very small operators. this is a small quantity of jet fuel relative to a typical operator's annual supply, deducted before the obligation applies.

### Fossil Fuel Proportion of Blended Fuel

Article 4(6) states: "Where fossil fuel is blended with other fuel, the fossil fuel proportion of the blended fuel is to be disregarded for the purposes of — (a) calculating the notional amount of relevant sustainable aviation fuel under paragraph (4); and (b) determining whether an amount of sustainable aviation fuel meets the sustainability criteria." *Source: Article 4(6), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Analytical inference:* This provision ensures that the compliance calculation credit applies only to the sustainable/relevant-feedstock portion of blended fuel, preventing double-counting.

### Hydrogen from Fossil Wastes — Carbon Capture Prerequisite

Article 2(2): "For hydrogen produced using wastes of fossil origin, that hydrogen is only to be considered a specified type of renewable transport fuel … if the carbon emitted during its production is captured and stored in a manner determined by the Administrator and published in guidance under article 14(1)(f)." *Source: Article 2(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### Double-Counting Prevention

A SAF certificate may not be issued where "the applicable sustainable aviation fuel, or a chemical precursor to it, has already been, and will not be, counted under a support scheme, or a United Kingdom renewable energy obligation other than the SAF obligation of the supplier." *Source: Article 16(3)(f), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

### Assumption of UK Supply — Displaceable Presumption

Article 4(1): "Subject to article 23(4), where it is shown that a person owns an amount of aviation fuel at the assessment time, it is presumed that that amount of fuel is supplied by that person at, or for delivery to, places in the United Kingdom at that time." Article 4(2): "The presumption in paragraph (1) is to be displaced only if the Administrator is satisfied that the fuel will not be supplied at, or for delivery to, places in the United Kingdom." *Source: Article 4(1)–(2), SAF Order 2024. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2024/9780348261714

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The rebuttable presumption means that a supplier owning aviation fuel in the UK at the assessment time bears the burden of demonstrating the fuel is not for UK supply. The evidentiary standard for displacing this presumption should be confirmed with legal counsel for entities involved in transit or re-export fuel arrangements.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Effective date slot (FACT):** "Released in 2011, the Scope 3 Standard is the only internationally accepted method for companies to account for these types of value chain emissions." **Jurisdictional scope slot (FACT):** "The Scope 3 Standard provides a methodology that can be used to account for and report emissions from companies of all sectors, globally." *Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard. https://ghgprotocol.org/standards/scope-3-standard

**Penalty summary and primary deadline:** the GHG Protocol is a voluntary accounting and reporting standard; the captured corpus states no penalty for non-adoption and no compliance deadline (see the Substantive Requirements section for the article-citing absence notes).

**Scope:** Air (primary), road (secondary), ocean (tertiary) across Americas–Europe–Asia lanes.
**Requirement:** A documented set of emission factors (kg CO₂e per tonne-kilometre) for each transport mode and, where feasible, by carrier and aircraft/vessel type.
**Deadline:** No regulatory deadline at the GHG Protocol standard level. Practical deadline: as client RFPs and CDP supplier surveys continue to arrive, the workspace needs this infrastructure before the next contract cycle in each vertical.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool. The workspace's current data infrastructure is not described in the input. If the workspace currently operates without a formal emission factor library tied to its booking systems, the gap is fundamental.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

*Analytical inference:* **Scope:** Per-shipment weight and distance data, by mode, for all booked freight.
**Requirement:** The standard's preferred calculation method (supplier-specific activity data) requires actual tonne-kilometres, not spend-based proxies.
**Deadline:** As above — no regulatory deadline at standard level; practical urgency driven by client demand cycle.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING — Prepare for client data requests using GHG Protocol-compliant emission factors.**
Action: Confirm that the workspace has documented, reproducible emission factors for air, road, and ocean freight on its primary trade lanes (Americas–Europe, Europe–Asia, Americas–Asia). Without this, the workspace cannot respond credibly to client Scope 3 data requests, cannot populate CDP supplier questionnaires on behalf of clients' procurement processes, and cannot meet RFP requirements that increasingly specify GHG Protocol-aligned transport emission data.
Cost: Internal staff time to build the methodology; no confirmed external cost figure available from the source pool. External cost of third-party verification is not publicly available from the source pool.
Affected verticals: All six cargo verticals. Highest immediate exposure: luxury goods, high-value automotive, live events (clients in these verticals are most likely to have CSRD or CDP obligations that trigger supplier data requests).
Why now: CSRD Phase 1 reporters (large EU-listed companies) are in an early reporting year. Supplier data requests tied to those reports are already materialising. *Source: EU CSRD (Directive 2022/2464/EU), applicable to large EU-listed companies for FY2024 — Legal Confirmation Required on exact scope of supplier data obligations.*

**MONITORING — Track GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard update process.**
Action: Assign a team member to monitor the GHG Protocol public consultation schedule. The GHG Protocol homepage (as reviewed for this brief) lists "Standards and Guidance Under Development" and "Public Consultations" as active navigation categories, indicating the update process is open. The scope and timeline of revisions are not confirmed in the available source pool.
Cost: Staff monitoring time only at this stage.
Affected verticals: All. If the update revises Category 4 calculation methodology, the workspace's client-facing emission reporting tools may require rebuilding.
Why now: Clients writing long-term sustainability commitments or RFP clauses that reference GHG Protocol methodology may be citing a standard that is in active revision. The workspace should not make long-term contractual commitments to a specific GHG Protocol version without understanding the revision timeline.

*Source for update process: GHG Protocol homepage, brief-preparation scrape, navigation item "Standards and Guidance Under Development." The specific scope of the update, its timeline, and any proposed changes to Scope 3 category definitions are NOT confirmed in the available source pool. This is a research gap.*

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The workspace's supply-chain role is freight forwarder. In GHG Protocol terms, this places the workspace in two positions simultaneously:

**Position A — Tier 1 supplier to cargo-principal clients.**
The workspace is a direct service provider to shippers (importers, exporters, manufacturers, distributors) across its six cargo verticals. Those clients, when preparing their Scope 3 inventories, must account for the emissions attributable to transport services they purchase. The workspace is the entity from which emission activity data (tonne-kilometres, fuel consumed, modal mix) must flow. The quality of the workspace's own emission records determines whether its clients can use primary data (higher quality under the standard) or must fall back to spend-based or average-data methods (lower quality, typically producing higher uncertainty in the client's disclosure).

*Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapter 7 (data quality hierarchy), WRI/WBCSD, 2011.*

**Position B — Reporting entity with its own Scope 3 obligations.**
If the workspace itself is subject to mandatory disclosure (CSRD, national equivalents, or voluntary CDP response), it must compile its own Scope 3 inventory. As a forwarder that does not operate its own aircraft, road fleet, or vessels at scale, the workspace's Scope 1 emissions are relatively low. Its Scope 3 — specifically the contracted carrier emissions attributable to cargo it books — may constitute the majority of its relevant GHG inventory.

**Legal Confirmation Required:** Whether the workspace qualifies as a "large undertaking" under CSRD, or is in scope under any national transposition of CSRD in its countries of registration, must be confirmed with legal counsel. This determination governs whether Position B obligations are mandatory or voluntary.

**Role placement note:** The workspace does not manufacture products, so Categories 11–15 (downstream, product-use related) are not material. The most material categories for a forwarder are Category 4 (upstream transport and distribution, i.e., carrier services purchased) and potentially Category 1 (purchased goods and services). *Legal Confirmation Required on materiality assessment.*

---

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

MONITORING

**GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard Update**
- **Event type:** Standards revision and public consultation
- **Issuing body:** GHG Protocol (WRI/WBCSD)
- **Expected date:** Not confirmed. The GHG Protocol homepage (as reviewed for this brief) lists "Standards and Guidance Under Development" and "Public Consultations" as active sections, and a formal update process has been announced. No publication date has been confirmed in the available source pool. *Research gap.*
- **Impact:** If category definitions are revised — particularly Categories 4 and 9, which are the most material for freight forwarders — the workspace's client-facing emission calculation tools and internal inventory methodology may require updating.
- **What the workspace should expect to decide:** Whether to participate in the public consultation process; whether to communicate the pending revision status to clients who are writing long-term sustainability clauses referencing GHG Protocol methodology.

*Source: GHG Protocol homepage, brief-preparation scrape. Navigation item "Standards and Guidance Under Development." No further specifics confirmed.*

**ISO/GHG Protocol Joint Working Group — Product-Level Accounting Standard**
- **Event type:** Joint standards development
- **Issuing body:** ISO and GHG Protocol jointly
- **Status:** GHG Protocol homepage (brief-preparation scrape) announces: "ISO and GHG Protocol Finalize Joint Working Group to Develop Product-Level Accounting Standard" (Announcement). Participants have been nominated. No draft or publication date confirmed.
- **Impact:** A product-level accounting standard could, once finalised, affect how emission intensity is attributed to individual shipments. Relevant to cargo verticals where clients seek per-unit or per-consignment emission certificates (luxury goods, fine art, high-value automotive).
- **What the workspace should expect to decide:** Whether to track this standard's development as a future procurement and reporting requirement, and whether product-level emission data capability should be built into the workspace's technology roadmap.

*Source: GHG Protocol homepage, brief-preparation scrape, announcement dated 09 April 2026.*

---

# 7. Threshold Questions

*Analytical inference:* The following definitional questions determine how and whether the GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard applies to the workspace's specific obligations. These are not legal opinions; they are compliance risk flags for legal and management review.

**Question 1: Is the workspace subject to any mandatory disclosure framework that requires GHG Protocol Scope 3 reporting?**
Status: Legal Confirmation Required. CSRD applicability depends on entity size, domicile, and listing status. SEC climate rule applicability is subject to ongoing litigation status as of this brief's date (the SEC's climate disclosure rule faced legal challenges; current enforcement status is not confirmed in the available source pool — Research Gap). National-level transpositions of CSRD vary by EU member state. *Source: EU CSRD (Directive 2022/2464/EU). SEC climate disclosure rule status requires legal confirmation.*

**Question 2: For Category 4 data provided to clients, does the workspace have sufficient operational data to supply primary activity data (tonne-kilometres and emission factors by mode) rather than spend-based estimates?**
Status: Operational gap assessment required. Primary activity data (mode, distance, weight, fuel type) is higher quality under the standard. If the workspace cannot provide this, clients will use secondary data sources, reducing client disclosure quality and potentially reducing the workspace's competitive position relative to forwarders that do provide primary data.

**Question 3: Does the standard's update (currently in progress) alter any category definitions or calculation methods material to the workspace?**
Status: Research gap. The scope of the update is not confirmed in the available source pool as of this brief's date.

---

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard is voluntary. The requirements below describe what the standard specifies for entities that adopt it or are required to report against it. They are not independently binding on the workspace absent a mandatory framework that incorporates them.*

## Scope 3 Category Identification and Screening

*Analytical inference:* The standard requires a reporting entity to screen all 15 Scope 3 categories and identify which are relevant based on size, influence, associated risks, and stakeholder expectations. A category is relevant if it contains emissions that are large in magnitude, contribute to climate-related financial risks, are considered important by key stakeholders, or are categories for which the entity can take action.

*Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapter 6, WRI/WBCSD, 2011.*

**Applied to the workspace:** For a freight forwarder, Category 4 (upstream transportation and distribution — carrier services purchased) is the likely dominant category by emission magnitude. The standard does not specify a threshold above which a category must be reported, but states that all relevant categories must be disclosed with an explanation for any omissions.

## Calculation Methodology Hierarchy

The standard defines four activity data types in descending order of preference: (1) supplier-specific activity data, (2) average-data methods using industry data, (3) hybrid methods, and (4) spend-based methods. Higher-quality data produces more accurate inventories. For a freight forwarder, supplier-specific data means obtaining actual fuel-consumption or tonne-kilometre data from each airline, road carrier, or ocean carrier used.

*Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapter 7, WRI/WBCSD, 2011.*

**Applied to the workspace:** The workspace's air-primary modal mix is operationally significant here. Aviation emission factors per tonne-kilometre are approximately 20–100× ocean freight depending on the route and calculation method. *Note: the specific multiplier range is sourced from industry-level estimates; the precise figures require verification against the workspace's actual carrier mix and route profile. This is labeled as a research gap pending carrier-specific data.*

## Reporting Boundaries and Base Year

The standard requires definition of an organizational boundary (equity share, financial control, or operational control) and a base year for inventory comparison. Changes to calculation methods that would materially alter the base year must trigger base year recalculation.

*Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapters 3–4, WRI/WBCSD, 2011.*

## Disclosure Requirements

For entities reporting under the standard, disclosures must include: total Scope 3 emissions by category; a description of types and activities included in each category; emission calculation methods; data sources; and any exclusions with justification.

*Source: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapter 11, WRI/WBCSD, 2011.*

*Operational implication:* the categories, methodology hierarchy and disclosure requirements above apply to entities that voluntarily adopt or are required by a mandatory framework to report against the Scope 3 Standard; the standard itself imposes no independent penalty or deadline.

No exceptions are stated in Sections 3 to 4, 6, 7 and 11 among the FACT claims attached above.

No scope limits are stated in Sections 3 to 4, 6, 7 and 11 among the FACT claims attached above.

Obligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 0.

Shortfall: no FACT claims are attached to this section in this repair pass -- its content is retained as descriptive paraphrase of the standard's own methodology chapters, not re-grounded to verbatim spans, since the pre-existing claims for this section could not be verified as attached (see discovery note).

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard does not itself establish a registration body or mandatory filing system. Reporting obligations are triggered by adopting frameworks:

*Analytical inference:* - **CDP:** Requires submission through the CDP platform. The workspace, if responding to CDP as a disclosed company or as a supplier in a client's supply chain survey, reports category-level Scope 3 data aligned to GHG Protocol definitions. CDP does not require a separate registration under the GHG Protocol.
- **CSRD/ESRS:** Requires inclusion in the annual sustainability statement filed with the relevant national competent authority in the EU. *Legal Confirmation Required on exact filing jurisdiction for the workspace.*
- **Voluntary disclosure:** No registration obligation under the standard itself.

*Source: GHG Protocol homepage, brief-preparation scrape. CDP supplier questionnaire process: general knowledge of CDP's public disclosure mechanism — this is sourced at tier 5 (industry body/platform); Legal Confirmation Required on specific CDP scoring criteria and how they apply to forwarder-category respondents.*

**Research gap:** No authoritative guidance specific to freight forwarders' Scope 3 registration or reporting requirements under any single mandatory framework has been confirmed from the available source pool. The FIATA sustainability working group and CLECAT have produced relevant guidance; these are identified as candidate sources in the New Sources Identified section below.

---

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Analytical inference:* The following describes what the workspace must build or have functional to satisfy GHG Protocol Scope 3 obligations — whether for its own reporting or to serve as a credible data supplier to clients.

## 1. Emission Factor Library by Mode and Lane

**Scope:** Air (primary), road (secondary), ocean (tertiary) across Americas–Europe–Asia lanes.
**Requirement:** A documented set of emission factors (kg CO₂e per tonne-kilometre) for each transport mode and, where feasible, by carrier and aircraft/vessel type.
**Deadline:** No regulatory deadline at the GHG Protocol standard level. Practical deadline: as client RFPs and CDP supplier surveys continue to arrive, the workspace needs this infrastructure before the next contract cycle in each vertical.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool. The workspace's current data infrastructure is not described in the input. If the workspace currently operates without a formal emission factor library tied to its booking systems, the gap is fundamental.

## 2. Tonne-Kilometre Activity Data Capture

**Scope:** Per-shipment weight and distance data, by mode, for all booked freight.
**Requirement:** The standard's preferred calculation method (supplier-specific activity data) requires actual tonne-kilometres, not spend-based proxies.
**Deadline:** As above — no regulatory deadline at standard level; practical urgency driven by client demand cycle.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool.

## 3. Client-Facing Emission Reporting Capability

**Scope:** All cargo verticals; highest near-term priority for luxury goods, live events, high-value automotive, and humanitarian (clients in these sectors most likely to have CSRD or CDP obligations).
**Requirement:** The ability to provide per-shipment or per-consignment CO₂e estimates to clients on demand or as part of a shipment documentation package.
**Deadline:** Competitive pressure exists now; no hard regulatory deadline at standard level.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool.

## 4. Carrier Data Procurement

**Scope:** Primary air carriers used on key lanes; road carriers; ocean carriers on tertiary lanes.
**Requirement:** Formal data-sharing arrangements or contractual provisions requiring carriers to provide fuel-consumption or certified emission factor data. Without this, the workspace can only use industry average factors, which are lower quality under the standard.
**Deadline:** No regulatory deadline at standard level.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** Not assessable from the available source pool.

---

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document provides a workspace-anchored intelligence brief on the principal green building certification standards applicable to logistics, warehouse, and distribution center assets. It synthesises coverage across five active frameworks — LEED (U.S. Green Building Council), BREEAM (BRE Group), NABERS (NSW Government / national Australia), ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager (U.S. EPA), and the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) — as they apply to the operation, certification, and mandatory compliance obligations affecting logistics real estate.

The workspace profile for this brief is a global freight forwarding operation with logistics and distribution infrastructure across Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific trade lanes, with air as primary transport mode and road as secondary. The workspace may occupy, lease, commission, or operate warehouse and distribution facilities. The brief does not address residential or pure-office assets except where threshold questions arise.

**Convention notes:**
- FACT citations appear inline at the end of each subsection.
- ANALYSIS is labeled *Analytical inference:*, *Industry interpretation:*, or *Operational implication:* at the sentence level.
- Items requiring legal review are labeled *Legal Confirmation Required:*.
- Severity labels are in SPACE-SEPARATED form.

**Dates:** Brief generated this brief's generation date.

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**Jurisdictional scope slot (FACT):** the MEES Regulations guidance page states: "Applies to England and Wales." *Source: MEES Regulations landlord guidance, GOV.UK. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

### The Landscape: Multiple Overlapping Frameworks

Green building certification for logistics facilities is not a single instrument. It is a landscape of voluntary certification schemes and mandatory statutory requirements that interact at the asset level. Workspaces operating or occupying logistics real estate must navigate both simultaneously.

**LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design)**

LEED is described as "the most widely recognized green building rating system in the world," offering "a framework for healthy, efficient, and cost-effective green buildings, providing environmental and social benefits" and serving as "a globally recognized symbol of sustainability leadership." *Source: LEED rating system, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/leed

LEED is structured for all building types and phases. For logistics assets specifically, LEED for Building Design and Construction (BD+C) "New Construction and Major Renovation is the most appropriate rating type for buildings that are new construction or major renovation," with the qualification that "at least 60% of the project's gross floor area must be complete by the time of certification and must include the entire building's gross floor area in the project." LEED for Operations and Maintenance (O+M): Existing Buildings "can be applied to existing buildings that are fully operational and occupied for at least one year" and "must include the entire building's gross floor area." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

As of March 2026, "there are almost 8,353 LEED‐certified and registered warehouse and distribution center projects representing over 2.94 billion square feet (273 million square meters) of built space." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

### LEED: Warehouse and Distribution Center Guidance

The USGBC has published specific guidance for warehouse and distribution center projects. Key provisions that apply to the logistics context:

**Speculative buildings:** "Many new build projects are speculative and do not have tenants contracted to occupy space. When tenant spaces are not under contract, the project may only be able to account for design and construction activities under the control of the owner and will not have details related to future tenant build-outs." For speculative logistics buildings, "LEED v4.1 BD+C presents more options as credit weightings are shifted to include more points that fall within the owner's control." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

**Process load challenge:** "Some warehouse and distribution center O+M projects can face challenges with process loads (energy, water, and waste) that can impact performance scores to the point that the prerequisites may not be met." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating high-throughput distribution centers with significant refrigeration, automation energy loads, or cold-chain infrastructure, the process load challenge is directly material. LEED prerequisite eligibility should be confirmed before committing to certification pursuit.

**LEED v5 and the Arc platform:** "LEED v5 is the most current version of the rating system and is available for all commercial projects pursuing certification under New Construction, Core and Shell, Commercial Interiors, and Existing Buildings." LEED v5 BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems "allow for all space types to certify utilizing the new Arc experience, which offers fluidity and flexibility for users. All performance, certification, and reporting will be delivered in one place." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

**LEED Volume Program:** "For organizations planning to certify several new construction projects, LEED volume certification can simplify LEED documentation and speed up the review process for those portfolios where uniformity and standardization of the LEED requirements are built into the project delivery process." This "offers valuable economies of scale for new construction buildings and commercial interior spaces." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

*Operational implication:* For workspaces managing a portfolio of owned or long-leased distribution facilities, the LEED Volume program reduces per-building documentation cost — the most relevant procurement structure for global logistics networks seeking portfolio-level ESG credentials.

**Campus guidance:** "Warehouse and distribution center projects commonly operate with multiple buildings spread across a single site under the control of a single entity. To address this, the LEED Campus Guidance developed. Its application to LEED projects represents the complexity and commonality of buildings and infrastructure on a shared site." *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

**Certification levels:** LEED certification levels are: Certified (40–49 points), Silver (50–59 points), Gold (60–79 points), Platinum (80+ points). *Source: LEED rating system, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/leed

### UK MEES: Cost Cap and Exemption Structure

For domestic properties, the MEES cost cap is stated as: "you are not currently required to spend more than £3,500 (including VAT) on energy efficiency improvements." If improvements cannot bring the property to EPC E within that cap, the landlord should "make all the improvements which can be made up to that amount, then register an 'all improvements made' exemption." *Source: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance, UK Government. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

The five exemption types available under MEES are: all relevant improvements made exemption; high cost exemption; wall insulation exemption; third-party consent exemption; property devaluation exemption; and temporary exemption due to recently becoming a landlord. All exemptions except the temporary exemption "last 5 years. After that it will expire and you must try again to improve the property's EPC rating to E." The temporary exemption "lasts 6 months from the date you became the landlord." *Source: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance, UK Government. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

# 8. Substantive Requirements

### A. NYC Mandatory Benchmarking (LL84/LL133)

Covered buildings in New York City: owners are required to use ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager to measure energy and water consumption and submit data to the City annually by May 1. The submission format is a Reporting Template "unique and specifically created through ESPM for each compliance year." *Source: Benchmarking and Energy Efficiency Rating - Buildings, NYC Department of Buildings. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page

Steps required:
1. Set up an account in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager (ESPM).
2. Enter building characteristics and uses. For buildings with a single/primary property use: "other or any variation of other will no longer be acceptable as a valid primary property type."
3. Collect "whole building energy and water data from the utilities (this data is automatically uploaded to the ESPM account by most utilities)."
4. Retrieve a Reporting Template and submit a benchmarking report.
5. Print and display the energy efficiency grade label "in a conspicuous location near each public entrance within 30 days after October 1 of every year."

*Source: Benchmarking and Energy Efficiency Rating - Buildings, NYC Department of Buildings. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page

**Exclusion:** "As of October 31, 2016, the term 'covered building' shall not include real property, not more than three stories, consisting of a series of attached, detached or semi-detached dwellings, for which ownership and the responsibility for maintenance of the HVAC systems and hot water heating systems is held by each individual dwelling unit owner, and with no HVAC system or hot water heating system in the series serving more than two dwelling units (also known as 'garden style' apartments)." This exclusion is residential and does not apply to logistics buildings. *Source: Benchmarking and Energy Efficiency Rating - Buildings, NYC Department of Buildings. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page

---

### B. EU EPBD — Non-Residential Trajectory

**Renovation obligations (trajectory):**
- By 2030: renovation of the worst-performing 16% of non-residential buildings (nationally determined thresholds).
- By 2033: renovation of the worst-performing 26% of non-residential buildings.
- Solar readiness: new buildings will need to be "solar-ready, meaning fit to host photovoltaic or solar thermal installations."
- Life-cycle GWP disclosure: phased in for new buildings >1,000 m², then more broadly; from January 2030 for all new buildings.
- Fossil fuel boilers: financial incentives ended for new stand-alone fossil fuel boilers from 1 January 2025.
- EV charging: recharging points for electric vehicles required in non-residential buildings; "recharging points will have to enable smart charging and, where appropriate, bi-directional charging."

*Source: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, European Commission DG Energy. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/topics/energy-efficiency/energy-efficient-buildings/energy-performance-buildings-directive_en

**Residential trajectory (for reference):** EU countries are to reduce average primary energy use of residential buildings across the Directive's implementation period. "At least 55% of the decrease of the average primary energy use is achieved through the renovation of the worst-performing buildings." This does not apply to logistics assets but sets the policy ambition context.

**Exemptions:** EU countries "can also exempt various categories of buildings from renovation requirements, including historical buildings and holiday homes." No express exemption for logistics assets is stated in the corpus source. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any Member State will exempt specific logistics asset classes from renovation obligations requires national counsel review.

*Source: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, European Commission DG Energy. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/topics/energy-efficiency/energy-efficient-buildings/energy-performance-buildings-directive_en

---

### C. UK MEES — EPC E Minimum (Domestic; Non-Domestic Requires Separate Confirmation)

For domestic properties covered by MEES: since 1 April 2020, EPC rating of E or above is required as a precondition to letting. The cost cap for improvements is £3,500 (including VAT). *Source: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance, UK Government. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

EPC recommendations table (illustrative from source, for domestic properties): The source provides a sample table showing improvement measures ranked by impact and cost, with indicative savings and post-improvement EPC ratings after each measure. Relevant categories for logistics (where analogous) include: insulation, heating system upgrades, draught proofing, low-energy lighting, solar photovoltaic panels. *Source: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance, UK Government. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

---

### D. LEED — Certification Point Requirements

To achieve LEED certification, a project "must first complete all prerequisites and then earn points by selecting and satisfying credit requirements. Projects go through a verification and review process by GBCI and are awarded points that correspond to a level of LEED certification: Certified, Silver, Gold and Platinum." *Source: LEED rating system, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/leed

For LEED v4.1 O+M, the rating system uses "legacy Arc, a state-of-the-art platform designed to collect, manage and benchmark your building across five performance categories: energy, water, waste, transportation, and human experience." The performance pathway enables recertification every 3 years. *Source: Applying LEED to warehouse and distribution center projects, U.S. Green Building Council. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/12089652865683-Applying-LEED-to-warehouse-and-distribution-center-projects

*Analytical inference:* BREEAM "support[s] ESG solutions in: Net zero carbon; Whole life performance; Health and social impact; Circularity and resilience; Biodiversity; Disclosures and reporting." BREEAM In-Use is the relevant standard for operating logistics facilities. Assessment involves a licensed BREEAM assessor evaluating the asset against the technical standard. *Source: Certification for Sustainable Buildings | BREEAM. https://www.breeam.com

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

### NYC LL84: Annual Submission to NYC DOB

- Submit benchmarking data via ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager to New York City by **May 1 annually**.
- If the May 1 deadline is missed: next quarterly deadline is August 1, then November 1, then February 1 of the following year.
- Submission confirmed by "a confirmation email from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Portfolio Manager that includes a date-stamped copy of data released to the city."
- Buildings must display the energy efficiency grade label annually, accessible in DOB NOW Public Portal from October 1; display required "within 30 days after October 1 of every year."

*Source: Benchmarking and Energy Efficiency Rating - Buildings, NYC Department of Buildings. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page

### UK MEES: PRS Exemptions Register

For domestic properties where an exemption applies, landlords register on the PRS Exemptions Register. Registration requires: address of property, type of exemption, landlord details, and exemption-specific evidence (quotes, surveyor reports, expert opinions as specified per exemption type). The Exemptions Register is publicly searchable. *Source: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance, UK Government. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/domestic-private-rented-property-minimum-energy-efficiency-standard-landlord-guidance

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an analogous exemptions register operates for non-domestic logistics leases requires counsel review.

### EU EPBD: National Energy Performance Databases

The EPBD requires that "data on the national building stock will become available via national energy performance databases." EPCs will become digital. *Source: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, European Commission DG Energy. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/topics/energy-efficiency/energy-efficient-buildings/energy-performance-buildings-directive_en The specific national registration and reporting formats are to be established through Member State transposition; these are not yet fully enacted as of this brief's generation date.

### LEED: Registration in Arc or LEED Online

LEED certification for BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems requires: register the project (LEED v5 in Arc; v4.1/v4 in LEED Online); choose credits; document and submit for review. *Source: LEED rating system, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/leed

### ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager: Account and Data Entry

To benchmark, a building owner or representative needs to "set up an account in the EPA's online tool, Energy Star Portfolio Manager (ESPM); enter building characteristics and uses; collect whole building energy and water data from the utilities." *Source: Benchmarking and Energy Efficiency Rating - Buildings, NYC Department of Buildings. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/benchmarking.page
